name: William Shakespeare
biography: English playwright, poet, and actor, widely regarded as the greatest writer in the English language. His works include 'Hamlet', 'Romeo and Juliet', and 'Macbeth'.

name: Jane Austen
biography: English novelist known for her romantic fiction and sharp social commentary. Her works, including 'Pride and Prejudice' and 'Sense and Sensibility', are cornerstones of English literature.

name: George Orwell
biography: English novelist and critic, known for his dystopian novel 'Nineteen Eighty-Four' and the allegorical 'Animal Farm'. His work is marked by lucid prose and opposition to totalitarianism.

name: J.R.R. Tolkien
biography: English writer, poet, and philologist, best known as the author of the high-fantasy works 'The Hobbit' and 'The Lord of the Rings', which created a new mythology.

name: Virginia Woolf
biography: English writer, considered one of the most important modernist authors of the 20th century. Known for novels like 'Mrs Dalloway' and 'To the Lighthouse' and her pioneering use of stream of consciousness.

name: Ernest Hemingway
biography: American novelist and short-story writer, known for his economical and understated style. A Nobel laureate, his works include 'The Old Man and the Sea' and 'A Farewell to Arms'.

name: Leo Tolstoy
biography: Russian writer who is regarded as one of the greatest authors of all time. He is best known for the novels 'War and Peace' and 'Anna Karenina,' which are pinnacles of realist fiction.

name: Fyodor Dostoevsky
biography: Russian novelist and philosopher. His works, including 'Crime and Punishment' and 'The Brothers Karamazov,' explore human psychology in the troubled political and social atmosphere of 19th-century Russia.

name: Gabriel García Márquez
biography: Colombian novelist and Nobel laureate, a pioneer of magical realism. He is best known for his novels 'One Hundred Years of Solitude' and 'Love in the Time of Cholera'.

name: Jorge Luis Borges
biography: Argentine short-story writer, essayist, and poet. His work embraces a character of unreality in all literature, exploring themes of labyrinths, mirrors, and dreams in works like 'Ficciones'.

name: Toni Morrison
biography: American novelist and Nobel laureate. Her work explores the Black American experience, particularly for Black women. Notable works include 'Beloved', 'Song of Solomon', and 'The Bluest Eye'.

name: Haruki Murakami
biography: Japanese writer whose books and stories have been bestsellers internationally. His work blends mundane reality with surreal elements, seen in 'Kafka on the Shore' and 'Norwegian Wood'.

name: Agatha Christie
biography: English writer known for her 66 detective novels featuring detectives Hercule Poirot and Miss Marple. The best-selling novelist of all time, she is the undisputed 'Queen of Crime'.

name: Stephen King
biography: American author of horror, supernatural fiction, and fantasy novels. Known as the 'King of Horror,' his prolific works include 'It,' 'The Shining,' and 'The Stand'.

name: J.K. Rowling
biography: British author of the 'Harry Potter' series, which has sold more than 500 million copies, becoming the best-selling book series in history and a global cultural phenomenon.

name: Edgar Allan Poe
biography: American writer, poet, and critic, best known for his tales of mystery and the macabre. He is a central figure of Romanticism and the inventor of the detective fiction genre.

name: Mary Shelley
biography: English novelist who wrote the Gothic novel 'Frankenstein,' a foundational text of science fiction. She also edited and promoted the works of her husband, Percy Bysshe Shelley.

name: James Joyce
biography: Irish novelist and poet, considered one of the most influential writers of the 20th century. His landmark work 'Ulysses' is noted for its experimental use of language and stream of consciousness.

name: Franz Kafka
biography: German-speaking Bohemian novelist. His work, like 'The Metamorphosis' and 'The Trial,' fuses elements of realism and the fantastic, giving rise to the term 'Kafkaesque'.

name: Albert Camus
biography: French philosopher, author, and journalist. A Nobel laureate, his works like 'The Stranger' and 'The Plague' contributed to the rise of the philosophy known as absurdism.

name: Isaac Asimov
biography: American writer and professor of biochemistry. A prolific writer of science fiction, he is known for the 'Foundation' series and his 'Three Laws of Robotics'.

name: Arthur C. Clarke
biography: British science-fiction writer, inventor, and futurist. Famous for co-writing the screenplay for '2001: A Space Odyssey' and his novels like 'Childhood's End'.

name: Philip K. Dick
biography: American writer whose science fiction explored philosophical and social themes. Many of his stories were adapted into films like 'Blade Runner' and 'Minority Report'.

name: Aldous Huxley
biography: English writer and philosopher. He wrote nearly fifty books but is best known for his dystopian novel 'Brave New World,' a chilling vision of a futuristic society.

name: Ray Bradbury
biography: American author who worked in a variety of genres, including fantasy, science fiction, and horror. Best known for his dystopian novel 'Fahrenheit 451'.

name: Ursula K. Le Guin
biography: American author known for her works of speculative fiction, including the 'Earthsea' fantasy series and the sci-fi novel 'The Left Hand of Darkness'. A pioneer for women in the genre.

name: Margaret Atwood
biography: Canadian poet, novelist, and literary critic. She is a prolific author of speculative fiction, with her most famous work being the dystopian novel 'The Handmaid's Tale'.

name: Chinua Achebe
biography: Nigerian novelist regarded as the dominant figure of modern African literature. His first novel 'Things Fall Apart' is a seminal work of post-colonial fiction.

name: Maya Angelou
biography: American poet, memoirist, and civil rights activist. She is best known for her 1969 memoir, 'I Know Why the Caged Bird Sings', a landmark in American literature.

name: Homer
biography: Legendary ancient Greek epic poet, traditionally said to be the author of the epic poems 'The Iliad' and 'The Odyssey,' foundational works of Western literature.

name: Dante Alighieri
biography: Italian poet, writer and philosopher. His 'Divine Comedy' is considered one of the most important poems of the Middle Ages and the greatest literary work in the Italian language.

name: Victor Hugo
biography: French poet, novelist, and dramatist of the Romantic movement. His best-known works are the epic novels 'Les Misérables' and 'The Hunchback of Notre-Dame'.

name: Jules Verne
biography: French novelist, poet, and playwright. A pioneer of the science fiction genre, he is known for his adventure novels like 'Journey to the Center of the Earth' and '20,000 Leagues Under the Seas'.

name: Subramania Bharati
biography: A pioneer of modern Tamil poetry, hailed as 'Mahakavi'. A freedom fighter and social reformer, his fiery patriotic and spiritual poems are legendary and inspirational.

name: Munshi Premchand
biography: A pioneer of modern Hindi and Urdu literature. Known as 'Upanyas Samrat' (Emperor among Novelists), his works like 'Godan' and 'Gaban' realistically depict the social and economic struggles of rural India.

name: R. K. Narayan
biography: A pioneer of Indian English literature, celebrated for his works set in the fictional South Indian town of Malgudi. His novels 'Swami and Friends' and 'The Guide' are classics.

name: M. T. Vasudevan Nair
biography: A towering figure in Malayalam literature. A novelist, screenwriter, and filmmaker, he has won the Jnanpith Award. His works include the classic novels 'Randamoozham' and 'Naalukettu'.

name: Kuvempu (K. V. Puttappa)
biography: A novelist, poet, and playwright, widely regarded as the greatest Kannada writer of the 20th century. He was the first Kannada writer to receive the Jnanpith Award for 'Sri Ramayana Darshanam'.

name: Gurazada Apparao
biography: A pioneer of modern Telugu literature. His play 'Kanyasulkam' is a masterpiece that satirized social evils. He championed spoken Telugu in writing, revolutionizing the language.

name: Mo Yan
biography: Chinese novelist and short story writer who won the 2012 Nobel Prize in Literature. He is known for his works of hallucinatory realism, such as 'Red Sorghum Clan'.

name: Plato
biography: Athenian philosopher during the Classical period in Ancient Greece. His Socratic dialogues and his work 'The Republic' are foundational texts of Western philosophy and political theory.

name: Aristotle
biography: Ancient Greek philosopher and scientist. A student of Plato, his writings on logic, ethics, politics, and metaphysics constitute the first comprehensive system of Western philosophy.

name: Virgil
biography: Ancient Roman poet of the Augustan period. He wrote three of the most famous poems in Latin literature: the Eclogues, the Georgics, and the epic Aeneid.

name: Ovid
biography: A Roman poet who lived during the reign of Augustus. He is best known for the 'Metamorphoses,' a mythological narrative poem, and for poems on love such as 'Ars Amatoria'.

name: Robert Kiyosaki
biography: American businessman and author, famous for the 'Rich Dad Poor Dad' series of personal finance books. His work advocates for financial literacy and building wealth through investment.

name: Dave Ramsey
biography: American personal finance personality and author. His books and radio show, including 'The Total Money Makeover,' provide a straightforward, step-by-step plan for getting out of debt.

name: Morgan Housel
biography: An American financial writer and author, best known for his book 'The Psychology of Money.' His work explores the behavioral aspects of finance and investing.

name: Adam Smith
biography: Scottish economist and philosopher known as the 'Father of Capitalism'. His 1776 book 'The Wealth of Nations' is a foundational text of modern economics.

name: John Maynard Keynes
biography: English economist whose ideas fundamentally changed the theory and practice of macroeconomics. His magnum opus, 'The General Theory of Employment, Interest and Money,' advocated for government intervention.

name: Milton Friedman
biography: American economist and Nobel laureate who promoted free-market capitalism. His work, including 'Capitalism and Freedom,' challenged the prevailing Keynesian consensus.

name: Seth Godin
biography: American author and marketing guru. His books, including 'Permission Marketing' and 'Purple Cow,' have reshaped modern marketing by focusing on ideas that spread and treating customers with respect.

name: Philip Kotler
biography: American marketing author and consultant, often called the 'Father of Modern Marketing.' His textbook, 'Marketing Management,' is a standard in universities worldwide.

name: Isaac Newton
biography: English mathematician, physicist, and astronomer. His book 'Philosophiæ Naturalis Principia Mathematica' laid the foundations for classical mechanics, universal gravitation, and calculus.

name: Albert Einstein
biography: German-born theoretical physicist who developed the theory of relativity, one of the two pillars of modern physics. His mass-energy equivalence formula E = mc² is world-famous.

name: Richard Feynman
biography: American theoretical physicist and Nobel laureate known for his work in quantum mechanics. His lectures, collected in 'The Feynman Lectures on Physics,' are a beloved educational resource.

name: Stephen Hawking
biography: English theoretical physicist and cosmologist. His book 'A Brief History of Time' became an international bestseller, making complex scientific ideas accessible to the public.

name: Marie Curie
biography: Polish and naturalized-French physicist and chemist who conducted pioneering research on radioactivity. She was the first woman to win a Nobel Prize and the only person to win in two different scientific fields.

name: Carl Sagan
biography: American astronomer and science communicator. His book and television series 'Cosmos' brought the wonders of the universe to a mass audience. A pioneer in the search for extraterrestrial intelligence.

name: Euclid
biography: Ancient Greek mathematician, often referred to as the 'Father of Geometry.' His work 'Elements' is one of the most influential works in the history of mathematics, serving as a textbook for millennia.

name: Srinivasa Ramanujan
biography: Indian mathematician who made extraordinary contributions to mathematical analysis, number theory, and continued fractions. A self-taught genius, his formulas are still being studied today.

name: Donald Knuth
biography: American computer scientist and mathematician. He is the author of the seminal multi-volume work 'The Art of Computer Programming,' a foundational text in the field of software algorithms.

name: Martin Fowler
biography: British software developer and author. His influential books, including 'Refactoring' and 'Patterns of Enterprise Application Architecture,' have shaped modern software design practices.

name: Robert C. Martin (Uncle Bob)
biography: American software engineer and author. A key figure in the Agile software movement, his books like 'Clean Code' and 'The Clean Coder' are essential reading for professional programmers.

name: Bjarne Stroustrup
biography: Danish computer scientist, most notable for the creation and development of the C++ programming language. His book 'The C++ Programming Language' is the standard reference for the language.

name: Andrew Ng
biography: A leading figure in artificial intelligence and machine learning. Co-founder of Coursera and a pioneer in online education, his lectures and papers have educated millions in the field of AI.

name: Geoffrey Hinton
biography: A cognitive psychologist and computer scientist known as one of the 'Godfathers of AI.' His pioneering work on artificial neural networks and deep learning has revolutionized the field.

name: Yann LeCun
biography: French computer scientist and a 'Godfather of AI.' His work on convolutional neural networks (CNNs) has been fundamental to modern computer vision and deep learning.

name: Werner Vogels
biography: The Chief Technology Officer at Amazon. His influential blog posts and whitepapers on distributed systems and cloud architecture have been foundational for modern cloud technology and engineering practices.

name: George R.R. Martin
biography: American novelist and screenwriter. He is best known for his epic fantasy series 'A Song of Ice and Fire,' which was adapted into the television series 'Game of Thrones'.

name: Neil Gaiman
biography: English author of novels, comic books, and graphic novels. His notable works include the comic book series 'The Sandman' and novels 'American Gods' and 'Coraline'.

name: Terry Pratchett
biography: English humorist and author of fantasy novels, especially comical works. He is best known for his 'Discworld' series of 41 novels, which satirize fantasy tropes and modern life.

name: Frank Herbert
biography: American science-fiction author best known for the 1965 novel 'Dune' and its sequels. The 'Dune' saga is a cornerstone of the genre, dealing with politics, religion, and ecology.

name: Arthur Conan Doyle
biography: British writer who created the character Sherlock Holmes. His detective stories are milestones in the field of crime fiction and have had a lasting impact on popular culture.

name: Gillian Flynn
biography: American writer of thriller and mystery novels. She is known for her dark, twisting plots and complex female characters, particularly in her bestselling novel 'Gone Girl'.

name: Nora Roberts
biography: A prolific American author of over 225 romance novels. She is one of the most popular and bestselling authors in the genre, also writing fantasy romance as J. D. Robb.

name: Julia Quinn
biography: American author of historical romance fiction, best known for her 'Bridgerton' series, which was adapted into a popular television show. Her work is celebrated for its wit and charm.

name: Hilary Mantel
biography: British writer whose work includes historical fiction, personal memoirs and short stories. She won the Booker Prize twice for 'Wolf Hall' and 'Bring Up the Bodies'.

name: H.P. Lovecraft
biography: American writer of weird and horror fiction, known for his creation of what became the Cthulhu Mythos. His work emphasizes cosmic horror and the insignificance of humanity.

name: Clive Cussler
biography: American adventure novelist and underwater explorer. His thriller novels, many featuring the character Dirk Pitt, are known for their fast-paced action and maritime adventures.

name: Kazuo Ishiguro
biography: British novelist of Japanese origin and Nobel laureate. His novels 'The Remains of the Day' and 'Never Let Me Go' explore themes of memory, identity, and regret with subtle prose.

name: Colson Whitehead
biography: American novelist. He is one of the few authors to win the Pulitzer Prize for Fiction twice, for his novels 'The Underground Railroad' and 'The Nickel Boys'.

name: Cixin Liu
biography: A prominent Chinese science fiction writer. His novel 'The Three-Body Problem' was the first Asian novel ever to win a Hugo Award and is a landmark of modern sci-fi.

name: Isabel Allende
biography: Chilean writer. Allende, whose works sometimes contain aspects of the 'magical realism' genre, is famous for novels such as 'The House of the Spirits' and 'City of the Beasts'.

name: Alan Moore
biography: English writer known for his influential work in comic books and graphic novels, including 'Watchmen,' 'V for Vendetta,' and 'From Hell.' He is a pioneer of the medium.

name: Art Spiegelman
biography: American cartoonist and editor best known for his graphic novel 'Maus,' a harrowing account of his father's experiences as a Holocaust survivor. It won a special Pulitzer Prize.

name: Anne Frank
biography: A German-born Jewish diarist. Her work, 'The Diary of a Young Girl,' documents her life in hiding during the German occupation of the Netherlands in World War II and is a testament to the human spirit.

name: Ron Chernow
biography: American writer and historian, known for his acclaimed biographies of historical figures. His biography 'Alexander Hamilton' inspired the hit Broadway musical 'Hamilton'.

name: Dale Carnegie
biography: American writer and lecturer and the developer of famous courses in self-improvement. His 1936 book, 'How to Win Friends and Influence People,' remains a bestseller.

name: Stephen Covey
biography: American educator and author. His book, 'The 7 Habits of Highly Effective People,' has sold more than 40 million copies worldwide and is a classic of the self-help genre.

name: Brené Brown
biography: American research professor and author. Her work on vulnerability, courage, and shame, presented in books like 'Daring Greatly,' has made her a prominent figure in modern self-help.

name: James Clear
biography: American author and speaker, best known for his book 'Atomic Habits.' His work focuses on building good habits and breaking bad ones through small, incremental changes.

name: Truman Capote
biography: American novelist and playwright. He is credited with creating the non-fiction novel genre with his book 'In Cold Blood,' a classic of the true crime genre.

name: Herodotus
biography: Ancient Greek writer and geographer credited with being the first historian. His work 'The Histories' is a detailed account of the Greco-Persian Wars.

name: Julia Child
biography: American chef, author, and television personality. Her debut cookbook, 'Mastering the Art of French Cooking,' is a seminal work that brought French cuisine to the American public.

name: Yotam Ottolenghi
biography: Israeli-English chef, restaurateur, and food writer. His cookbooks, such as 'Plenty' and 'Jerusalem,' are celebrated for their focus on vegetables and vibrant Middle Eastern flavors.

name: Bill Bryson
biography: American-British author of humorous books on travel, as well as books on the English language and science. His work 'A Short History of Nearly Everything' is a celebrated classic.

name: Jack Kerouac
biography: American novelist and poet, a pioneer of the Beat Generation. His novel 'On the Road' became an American classic, defining a generation and inspiring countless travelers.

name: F. Scott Fitzgerald
biography: American novelist whose works illustrate the Jazz Age. 'The Great Gatsby' is widely considered his magnum opus, exploring themes of wealth, class, and the American Dream.

name: William Faulkner
biography: American writer and Nobel laureate from Mississippi. A key figure in Southern literature, he is known for his novels 'The Sound and the Fury' and 'As I Lay Dying'.

name: Kurt Vonnegut
biography: American writer known for his satirical and darkly humorous novels. 'Slaughterhouse-Five' blends science fiction and satire to critique war and modern society.

name: John Steinbeck
biography: American author and Nobel Prize winner. He wrote 27 books, most famously 'The Grapes of Wrath' and 'Of Mice and Men,' which examine the lives of the working class.

name: Herman Melville
biography: American novelist, short story writer, and poet of the American Renaissance period. Best known for his epic novel 'Moby-Dick,' a tale of obsession and revenge.

name: Mark Twain
biography: American writer and humorist lauded as the 'greatest humorist the United States has produced.' Known for 'The Adventures of Tom Sawyer' and 'Adventures of Huckleberry Finn'.

name: Charles Dickens
biography: English writer and social critic. He created some of the world's best-known fictional characters and is regarded as the greatest novelist of the Victorian era. Wrote 'A Tale of Two Cities'.

name: Anton Chekhov
biography: Russian playwright and short-story writer who is considered to be among the greatest writers of short fiction in history. His principal plays include 'The Seagull' and 'The Cherry Orchard'.

name: Vladimir Nabokov
biography: Russian-American novelist, poet, and entomologist. His most famous and controversial novel, 'Lolita,' is celebrated for its complex wordplay and prose style.

name: Simone de Beauvoir
biography: French writer, intellectual, and feminist philosopher. Her 1949 treatise 'The Second Sex' is a foundational text of second-wave feminism.

name: Marcel Proust
biography: French novelist, critic, and essayist who wrote the monumental novel 'In Search of Lost Time'. His work is known for its exploration of involuntary memory and the passage of time.

name: Alexandre Dumas
biography: French writer. Many of his historical novels of high adventure were originally published as serials, including 'The Count of Monte Cristo' and 'The Three Musketeers'.

name: Johann Wolfgang von Goethe
biography: German writer and statesman. His works include epic and lyric poetry, prose and verse dramas, and memoirs. His masterpiece is the two-part drama 'Faust'.

name: Hermann Hesse
biography: German-born Swiss poet, novelist, and painter. His best-known works include 'Siddhartha' and 'Steppenwolf,' which explore an individual's search for authenticity and spirituality.

name: Italo Calvino
biography: Italian journalist and writer of short stories and novels. His works, like 'Invisible Cities' and 'If on a winter's night a traveler,' are known for their playful, postmodern style.

name: Umberto Eco
biography: Italian medievalist, philosopher, and novelist. He is best known for his groundbreaking 1980 historical mystery novel 'The Name of the Rose'.

name: Yukio Mishima
biography: Japanese author, poet, and nationalist. Mishima is considered one of the most important Japanese authors of the 20th century, known for 'The Temple of the Golden Pavilion'.

name: Yasunari Kawabata
biography: Japanese novelist whose spare, lyrical prose won him the Nobel Prize in Literature in 1968, the first Japanese author to receive the award. Wrote 'Snow Country'.

name: Lu Xun
biography: The leading figure of modern Chinese literature. His works, including 'A Madman's Diary' and 'The True Story of Ah Q,' were sharp, critical attacks on the old social order.

name: Rumi
biography: 13th-century Persian poet, Islamic scholar, and Sufi mystic. His poems have been widely translated and are celebrated for their themes of love, spirituality, and divine connection.

name: Arundhati Roy
biography: Indian author and activist best known for her novel 'The God of Small Things,' which won the Man Booker Prize for Fiction in 1997. Her work often critiques global politics and social issues.

name: Vikram Seth
biography: Indian novelist and poet. He is widely known for his epic novel 'A Suitable Boy', one of the longest novels ever published in a single volume in the English language.

name: Amitav Ghosh
biography: Acclaimed writer whose work often features historical settings. His notable works include 'The Glass Palace' and the 'Ibis' trilogy. Awarded the 54th Jnanpith award.

name: Jhumpa Lahiri
biography: American author of Indian origin. Her debut collection, 'Interpreter of Maladies,' won the Pulitzer Prize for Fiction. Her works explore the immigrant experience and cultural identity.

name: Shashi Tharoor
biography: Indian politician and acclaimed writer. He has authored numerous fiction and non-fiction works, including 'The Great Indian Novel' and 'An Era of Darkness,' known for his eloquent prose.

name: Aravind Adiga
biography: Indo-Australian writer whose debut novel, 'The White Tiger,' won the 2008 Man Booker Prize. His works offer a dark, humorous perspective on class struggle in modern India.

name: Ruskin Bond
biography: Beloved Indian author of British descent, known for his children's books and stories set in the Himalayan foothills. He received the Sahitya Akademi Award and the Padma Bhushan.

name: Khushwant Singh
biography: Prominent Indian author, journalist, and politician. His classic novel 'Train to Pakistan' vividly recounts the Partition of India. Known for his secularism, humor, and sharp wit.

name: Harivansh Rai Bachchan
biography: A notable poet of the Chhayavaad literary movement in Hindi literature. He is best known for his epic poem 'Madhushala'. He was also the father of Bollywood superstar Amitabh Bachchan.

name: Mahadevi Varma
biography: A leading poet of the Chhayavaad movement, often called the 'modern Meera'. Her poignant poetry and prose, including 'Yama', earned her the Jnanpith Award.

name: Ramdhari Singh 'Dinkar'
biography: A celebrated Hindi poet, essayist, and patriot, hailed as a 'Rashtrakavi' (National Poet). His epic poems 'Rashmirathi' and 'Kurukshetra' are known for their heroic and nationalist fervor.

name: Kalki Krishnamurthy
biography: A celebrated Tamil writer and freedom fighter. He is renowned for his historical magnum opus, 'Ponniyin Selvan,' an epic novel set in the Chola dynasty. He mastered the art of serialized fiction.

name: Vaikom Muhammad Basheer
biography: A legendary Malayalam fiction writer, known for his simple, humorous, and deeply humane stories. Hailed as the 'Beypore Sultan', his works like 'Pathummayude Aadu' are beloved classics.

name: U. R. Ananthamurthy
biography: A leading figure of the 'Navya' (modernist) movement in Kannada literature. His novel 'Samskara' is a classic. A finalist for the Man Booker International Prize and a Jnanpith Award recipient.

name: Sri Sri (Srirangam Srinivasa Rao)
biography: A revolutionary poet who introduced new forms of expression in Telugu literature. His collection 'Maha Prasthanam' is a landmark of progressive poetry, inspiring generations of writers.

name: Jiddu Krishnamurti
biography: An Indian philosopher, speaker, and writer. He maintained that he belonged to no nationality or religion and was not a guru, but spoke on subjects such as psychological revolution and the nature of mind.

name: Paramahansa Yogananda
biography: An Indian monk, yogi, and guru who introduced millions to the teachings of meditation and Kriya Yoga. His book, 'Autobiography of a Yogi,' is a spiritual classic.

name: Wernher von Braun
biography: A German and later American aerospace engineer. A leading figure in the development of rocket technology, from the V-2 rocket for Nazi Germany to the Saturn V for NASA's Apollo program.

name: Sun Tzu
biography: Chinese general, strategist, and philosopher credited as the author of 'The Art of War,' an influential work of military strategy that has affected both military thinking and business tactics.

name: Niccolò Machiavelli
biography: Italian diplomat, philosopher, and writer. He is best known for his political treatise 'The Prince,' which advises rulers on how to gain and maintain power, giving rise to the term 'Machiavellian'.

name: James Baldwin
biography: American writer and activist. His essays, such as in 'Notes of a Native Son,' and novels like 'Go Tell It on the Mountain,' explore intricate racial, sexual, and class distinctions in America.

name: Langston Hughes
biography: American poet, social activist, novelist, and playwright. He was one of the earliest innovators of the literary art form called jazz poetry and a leader of the Harlem Renaissance.

name: Zora Neale Hurston
biography: American author, anthropologist, and filmmaker. She was a leader of the Harlem Renaissance, best known for her 1937 novel 'Their Eyes Were Watching God'.

name: Alice Walker
biography: American novelist, short story writer, and activist. She wrote the critically acclaimed novel 'The Color Purple,' for which she won the Pulitzer Prize for Fiction.

name: Octavia E. Butler
biography: An American science fiction author. A multiple recipient of the Hugo and Nebula awards, her works like 'Kindred' and 'Parable of the Sower' explored themes of race, power, and humanity.

name: N. K. Jemisin
biography: An American science fiction and fantasy writer. She is the first author to win the Hugo Award for Best Novel in three consecutive years for her 'Broken Earth' series.

name: Chimamanda Ngozi Adichie
biography: Nigerian writer whose works range from novels to short stories. She is a prominent feminist voice and is known for 'Americanah,' 'Half of a Yellow Sun,' and the essay 'We Should All Be Feminists'.

name: Wole Soyinka
biography: A Nigerian playwright, novelist, and poet. He was awarded the 1986 Nobel Prize in Literature, the first sub-Saharan African to be honored in that category. Known for works like 'The Lion and the Jewel'.

name: Naguib Mahfouz
biography: An Egyptian writer who won the 1988 Nobel Prize in Literature. He is regarded as one of the first contemporary writers of Arabic literature to explore themes of existentialism. Wrote 'The Cairo Trilogy'.

name: Orhan Pamuk
biography: A Turkish novelist and Nobel laureate. His work often deals with themes of identity, memory, and the clash between East and West. His novels include 'My Name Is Red' and 'The Museum of Innocence'.

name: Milan Kundera
biography: A Czech-born French writer. He is best known for his novel 'The Unbearable Lightness of Being,' which explores the lives of artists and intellectuals in the shadow of the Prague Spring.

name: Elena Ferrante
biography: The pseudonymous Italian novelist behind the critically acclaimed 'Neapolitan Novels' series. Her work explores female friendship, class, and the complex social fabric of Naples.

name: Karl Ove Knausgård
biography: A Norwegian author known for his six-volume autobiographical novel series 'My Struggle' ('Min Kamp'), a work of monumental detail about his own life and thoughts.

name: Sally Rooney
biography: An Irish author and screenwriter. Her novels, including 'Normal People' and 'Conversations with Friends,' have received critical acclaim for their portrayal of modern relationships and class.

name: George Saunders
biography: An American writer of short stories, essays, and novels. He is known for his satirical and often surreal style. His novel 'Lincoln in the Bardo' won the 2017 Booker Prize.

name: Ted Chiang
biography: An American science fiction author. He is known for his intellectually rigorous and philosophically deep short stories. His story 'Story of Your Life' was the basis for the film 'Arrival'.

name: Brandon Sanderson
biography: An American author of epic fantasy and science fiction. He is best known for the 'Cosmere' fictional universe, in which most of his fantasy novels, like the 'Mistborn' series, are set.

name: Patrick Rothfuss
biography: An American writer of epic fantasy. He is the author of the ongoing series 'The Kingkiller Chronicle,' which has garnered a massive and dedicated fanbase.

name: Suzanne Collins
biography: An American television writer and novelist, best known as the author of the bestselling young adult dystopian series 'The Hunger Games'.

name: Veronica Roth
biography: An American novelist and short story writer, known for her debut dystopian trilogy 'Divergent,' which became a bestseller and was adapted into a successful film series.

name: Michelle Obama
biography: Former First Lady of the United States. Her 2018 memoir, 'Becoming,' was a critical and commercial success, chronicling her life from childhood to her time in the White House.

name: Yuval Noah Harari
biography: An Israeli historian and author. He is known for his international bestsellers 'Sapiens: A Brief History of Humankind,' 'Homo Deus: A Brief History of Tomorrow,' and '21 Lessons for the 21st Century'.

name: Tara Westover
biography: An American memoirist and historian. Her memoir 'Educated' chronicles her life growing up in a fundamentalist family in rural Idaho and her subsequent journey to higher education.

name: Michelle Zauner
biography: An American musician and author, known as the lead vocalist of the band Japanese Breakfast. Her 2021 memoir, 'Crying in H Mart,' received critical acclaim for its exploration of grief and identity.

name: Eric Carle
biography: An American author and illustrator of children's books. His picture book, 'The Very Hungry Caterpillar,' is a classic, celebrated for its collage-style illustrations and educational themes.

name: J. D. Salinger
biography: An American writer known for his novel 'The Catcher in the Rye.' A classic of adolescent angst and rebellion, the book made him a literary icon, after which he became famously reclusive.

name: Emily Dickinson
biography: American poet. A reclusive figure, her powerful and innovative poetry was mostly unpublished during her lifetime. Her work challenges conventional definitions of poetry.

name: Walt Whitman
biography: American poet and essayist. A humanist, he was a part of the transition between transcendentalism and realism. He is best known for his poetry collection 'Leaves of Grass'.

name: Robert Frost
biography: An American poet. His work was initially published in England before it was in the United States. He is highly regarded for his realistic depictions of rural life and his command of American colloquial speech.

name: Sylvia Plath
biography: An American poet and novelist. She is credited with advancing the genre of confessional poetry and is best known for her novel 'The Bell Jar' and her poetry collections 'Ariel' and 'The Colossus'.

name: Charles Bukowski
biography: A German-American poet, novelist, and short story writer. His writing was influenced by the social and cultural ambiance of Los Angeles, focusing on the lives of poor Americans in a raw, direct style.

name: Pablo Neruda
biography: A Chilean poet-diplomat and politician who won the Nobel Prize for Literature in 1971. He wrote in a variety of styles, including surrealist poems, historical epics, and passionate love poems.

name: Federico García Lorca
biography: A Spanish poet, playwright, and theatre director. A prominent member of the Generation of '27, he is considered one of Spain's most important literary figures. Known for plays like 'Blood Wedding'.

name: Rainer Maria Rilke
biography: A Bohemian-Austrian poet and novelist. He is considered one of the most significant poets in the German language, known for his lyrical intensity and mystical themes in works like 'Duino Elegies'.

name: Charles Baudelaire
biography: A French poet who also produced notable work as an essayist and art critic. His most famous work, 'Les Fleurs du mal' (The Flowers of Evil), expresses the changing nature of beauty in modern Paris.

name: Arthur Rimbaud
biography: A French poet who was a key figure in the Symbolist movement. He produced his best-known works while still in his late teens. His work influenced modern literature, music, and art.

name: Fernando Pessoa
biography: A Portuguese poet, writer, and philosopher, described as one of the most significant literary figures of the 20th century. He wrote under numerous heteronyms, most famously in 'The Book of Disquiet'.

name: Thomas Pynchon
biography: An American novelist. A MacArthur Fellow, he is noted for his dense and complex novels. His best-known works are 'Gravity's Rainbow' and 'The Crying of Lot 49'.

name: David Foster Wallace
biography: An American author of novels, short stories and essays. Wallace is best known for his 1996 novel 'Infinite Jest,' widely cited as one of the greatest literary works of the 20th century.

name: Cormac McCarthy
biography: American novelist. He has written ten novels in the Southern Gothic, Western, and post-apocalyptic genres. He is well known for 'The Road' and 'Blood Meridian'.

name: Don DeLillo
biography: American novelist, short story writer, and playwright. His works have covered subjects as diverse as television, nuclear war, and language. Known for 'White Noise' and 'Underworld'.

name: Philip Roth
biography: American novelist and short-story writer. Roth's fiction, regularly set in Newark, New Jersey, is known for its intensely autobiographical character. Known for 'Portnoy's Complaint'.

name: Ayn Rand
biography: Russian-born American writer and philosopher. She is known for her novels 'The Fountainhead' and 'Atlas Shrugged,' and for developing a philosophical system she named Objectivism.

name: Thomas Mann
biography: A German novelist and Nobel laureate. His highly symbolic and ironic epic novels are noted for their insight into the psychology of the artist and the intellectual. Wrote 'The Magic Mountain'.

name: Albert Schweitzer
biography: A French-German theologian, musician, philosopher, and physician. He received the Nobel Peace Prize for his philosophy of 'Reverence for Life'. He founded a hospital in Lambaréné, Gabon.

name: W. G. Sebald
biography: A German writer and academic. His works, which blend fiction, history, and memoir with melancholic photographs, are largely concerned with themes of memory, loss, and decay. Wrote 'The Rings of Saturn'.

name: Günter Grass
biography: A German novelist, poet, playwright, and Nobel laureate. He is best known for his first novel, 'The Tin Drum,' a key text in European magical realism.

name: Murasaki Shikibu
biography: A Japanese novelist and poet at the Imperial court during the Heian period. She is best known as the author of 'The Tale of Genji,' widely considered to be the world's first novel.

name: Kenzaburō Ōe
biography: A Japanese writer and a major figure in contemporary Japanese literature. His works deal with political, social and philosophical issues, including nuclear weapons. He won the Nobel Prize in 1994.

name: Ryūnosuke Akutagawa
biography: Japanese writer active in the Taishō period. Regarded as the 'Father of the Japanese short story,' his famous works like 'Rashomon' and 'In a Grove' explore human nature and morality.

name: H. G. Wells
biography: An English writer. Prolific in many genres, he is now best remembered for his science fiction novels and is often called the 'father of science fiction'. Wrote 'The Time Machine' and 'The War of the Worlds'.

name: George Eliot
biography: The pen name of Mary Ann Evans, an English novelist, poet, and journalist. She was a leading writer of the Victorian era, known for her psychological insight in novels like 'Middlemarch'.

name: The Brontë Sisters
biography: A nineteenth-century literary family. Charlotte wrote 'Jane Eyre,' Emily wrote 'Wuthering Heights,' and Anne wrote 'The Tenant of Wildfell Hall,' all of which are classics of English literature.

name: Leo Babauta
biography: A Guamanian-American author and blogger known for his minimalist lifestyle and productivity blog, 'Zen Habits.' His books, like 'The Power of Less,' focus on simplicity and habit formation.

name: Angela Duckworth
biography: An American academic, psychologist, and author. She is known for her book 'Grit: The Power of Passion and Perseverance,' which argues that grit is a key predictor of success.

name: Carol S. Dweck
biography: An American psychologist known for her work on the mindset psychological trait. Her book 'Mindset: The New Psychology of Success' explores the power of having a growth mindset.

name: Adam Grant
biography: An American psychologist and author. A top-rated professor at the Wharton School, his books, including 'Give and Take' and 'Originals,' explore work and psychology.

name: Malcolm Gladwell
biography: A Canadian journalist and author. His popular books, such as 'The Tipping Point' and 'Outliers,' explore social sciences and psychology through compelling storytelling.

name: Daniel Kahneman
biography: An Israeli-American psychologist and economist. A Nobel laureate, his book 'Thinking, Fast and Slow' summarizes his research on cognitive biases and behavioral economics.

name: Niccolò di Bernardo dei Machiavelli
biography: An Italian diplomat and writer. He is best known for 'The Prince,' a political treatise that offers pragmatic, often ruthless, advice on acquiring and maintaining political power.

name: David McCullough
biography: An American author and historian. A two-time winner of the Pulitzer Prize, he is known for his popular and critically acclaimed biographies of figures like John Adams and Truman.

name: Robert Caro
biography: An American journalist and author known for his monumental biographies of Robert Moses ('The Power Broker') and Lyndon B. Johnson ('The Years of Lyndon Johnson').

name: Doris Kearns Goodwin
biography: An American biographer, historian, and political commentator. She won the Pulitzer Prize for History for 'No Ordinary Time: Franklin and Eleanor Roosevelt'.

name: Samin Nosrat
biography: An American chef and food writer. Her 2017 cookbook, 'Salt, Fat, Acid, Heat: Mastering the Elements of Good Cooking,' became a bestseller and was adapted into a Netflix series.

name: J. Kenji López-Alt
biography: An American chef and food writer. His book 'The Food Lab: Better Home Cooking Through Science' uses a scientific approach to explore and explain cooking techniques.

name: Anthony Bourdain
biography: An American celebrity chef, author, and travel documentarian. His 2000 book 'Kitchen Confidential' was a bestselling exposé of the restaurant world. He explored international culture and cuisine in his TV shows.

name: Jon Krakauer
biography: An American writer and mountaineer. He is the author of bestselling non-fiction books, including 'Into Thin Air,' 'Into the Wild,' and 'Under the Banner of Heaven'.

name: Laura Hillenbrand
biography: An American author of non-fiction. She is known for her bestselling books 'Seabiscuit: An American Legend' and 'Unbroken: A World War II Story of Survival, Resilience, and Redemption'.

name: Erik Larson
biography: An American journalist and author of narrative non-fiction. He is known for his book 'The Devil in the White City,' which interweaves the stories of the 1893 World's Fair and a serial killer.

name: Mary Roach
biography: An American author specializing in popular science. She is known for her humor and curiosity in books like 'Stiff: The Curious Lives of Human Cadavers' and 'Gulp'.

name: Rabindranath Tagore
biography: A Bengali polymath who reshaped literature and music. The first non-European to win the Nobel Prize in Literature (1913) for his collection 'Gitanjali'. He was a poet, writer, composer, and painter.

name: Mahasweta Devi
biography: An Indian writer and activist. Her works, including 'Hajar Churashir Maa' and 'Rudali', focus on the brutal oppression of tribal communities and the marginalized by powerful forces.

name: Bankim Chandra Chatterjee
biography: A key figure in the Bengali literary renaissance. He wrote the novel 'Anandamath,' which was a source of inspiration for freedom fighters and included the national song 'Vande Mataram'.

name: Satyajit Ray
biography: While a legendary filmmaker, he was also a prolific writer, creating the iconic detective 'Feluda' and scientist 'Professor Shonku'. His writings are a treasure of Bengali children's and popular literature.

name: Sunil Gangopadhyay
biography: A prominent Indian poet and novelist. His historical novel 'Sei Samay' received the Sahitya Akademi Award. He wrote in a variety of genres, from poetry to children's fiction.

name: Saadat Hasan Manto
biography: A pioneering Urdu writer, known for his stark and controversial short stories. His work, like 'Toba Tek Singh,' vividly captured the human tragedy of the Partition of India.

name: Ismat Chughtai
biography: An eminent Urdu fiction writer. A feminist voice, her short story 'Lihaaf' (The Quilt) was met with controversy for its exploration of female sexuality. She was a recipient of the Padma Shri.

name: V. S. Khandekar
biography: A major Marathi writer and a Jnanpith Award recipient. His novel 'Yayati' is a celebrated classic that reinterprets a story from the Mahabharata to explore themes of desire and sacrifice.

name: Shivaji Sawant
biography: A renowned Marathi novelist, best known for his mythological and historical novels. His works 'Mrityunjay' (on Karna) and 'Chhava' (on Sambhaji) are modern classics of the genre.

name: Amrita Pritam
biography: An eminent Punjabi writer and poet. The first woman to win the Sahitya Akademi Award, her poignant poem on the Partition, 'Ajj Aakhaan Waris Shah Nu,' is an immortal classic.

name: Confucius
biography: A Chinese philosopher whose teachings, preserved in the 'Analects,' have deeply influenced Chinese, Korean, Japanese, and Vietnamese thought and life. His philosophy emphasized personal and governmental morality.

name: Laozi
biography: An ancient Chinese philosopher and writer. He is the reputed author of the 'Tao Te Ching,' the founder of philosophical Taoism, and a deity in religious Taoism.

name: Sophocles
biography: One of three ancient Greek tragedians whose plays have survived. His best-known tragedies feature Oedipus and Antigone and are collectively known as the Theban plays.

name: Euripides
biography: A tragedian of classical Athens. He is one of the few ancient Greek playwrights whose plays have survived in large numbers. Known for works like 'Medea' and 'The Bacchae'.

name: Seneca the Younger
biography: A Roman Stoic philosopher, statesman, and dramatist. His philosophical works and letters, such as 'On the Shortness of Life,' are cornerstones of Stoic philosophy.

name: Marcus Aurelius
biography: Roman emperor and Stoic philosopher. His private collection of thoughts and notes, 'Meditations,' is a significant work of Stoic philosophy, offering timeless guidance on self-discipline and virtue.

name: Thomas Sowell
biography: An American economist and social theorist. A senior fellow at the Hoover Institution, his writings, including 'Basic Economics,' champion free-market principles with clarity and rigor.

name: Nassim Nicholas Taleb
biography: A Lebanese-American essayist and scholar whose work focuses on problems of randomness and uncertainty. He is the author of the 'Incerto' series, which includes 'The Black Swan'.

name: Al Ries
biography: An American marketing professional and author. He, along with Jack Trout, co-authored the classic 'Positioning: The Battle for Your Mind,' a foundational text in marketing strategy.

name: Daniel H. Pink
biography: An American author who has written several bestselling books about business, work, and behavior. His works include 'Drive: The Surprising Truth About What Motivates Us' and 'To Sell Is Human'.

name: Jerry J. Weygandt
biography: An American accounting academic and author. He is the primary author of 'Financial Accounting,' one of the most widely used introductory accounting textbooks in the world.

name: Donald E. Kieso
biography: An American academic who, along with Jerry Weygandt, co-authored 'Intermediate Accounting,' a landmark textbook that has educated generations of accounting professionals.

name: Tom Wheelwright
biography: An American CPA and author, known for his book 'Tax-Free Wealth.' As a Rich Dad Advisor, his work focuses on legal strategies for tax reduction for investors and business owners.

name: William D. Cohan
biography: An American journalist and author who specializes in writing about Wall Street and high finance. His books, like 'House of Cards,' provide inside accounts of major financial institutions.

name: Elon Musk
biography: While a technologist and entrepreneur, his numerous whitepapers, presentations, and published plans for SpaceX, Tesla, and Neuralink serve as foundational texts in modern space, EV, and AI technology.

name: Robert Zubrin
biography: An American aerospace engineer and author, best known for his advocacy for the human exploration of Mars. His book 'The Case for Mars' laid out a detailed, low-cost plan for a crewed mission.

name: Antoine de Saint-Exupéry
biography: A French writer, poet, and pioneering aviator. He is best remembered for his novella 'The Little Prince' and for his lyrical aviation writings, including 'Wind, Sand and Stars'.

name: Dmitry Glukhovsky
biography: A Russian author and journalist, best known for his science fiction novel 'Metro 2033,' which spawned a successful video game franchise. His work often explores post-apocalyptic themes.

name: Stanisław Lem
biography: A Polish writer of science fiction and essays on philosophy. He is best known for his novel 'Solaris.' His work often explores philosophical themes and the limitations of human understanding.

name: Andrzej Sapkowski
biography: A Polish fantasy writer. He is best known for his book series 'The Witcher,' which has been adapted into a popular series of video games and a television show.

name: Michael Ende
biography: A German writer of fantasy and children's fiction. His most famous works are 'The Neverending Story' and 'Momo,' which are celebrated for their imagination and philosophical depth.

name: Robert Jordan
biography: The pen name of James Oliver Rigney Jr., an American writer of epic fantasy. He is best known for his sprawling 'The Wheel of Time' series, a landmark of the genre.

name: Robin Hobb
biography: The pen name of Margaret Astrid Lindholm Ogden, an American writer. She is best known for her fantasy novels set in the 'Realm of the Elderlings,' beginning with the 'Farseer Trilogy'.

name: Raymond Chandler
biography: An American-British novelist and screenwriter. He was a founder of the hardboiled school of detective fiction. His protagonist, Philip Marlowe, is an iconic private eye.

name: Dashiell Hammett
biography: An American author of hardboiled detective novels and short stories. He created iconic characters like Sam Spade ('The Maltese Falcon') and the Continental Op.

name: Tana French
biography: An Irish-American writer and theatrical actress. Her 'Dublin Murder Squad' series of psychological mystery novels has received widespread critical acclaim.

name: Lee Child
biography: The pen name of James Dover Grant, a British author of thriller novels. He is best known for his 'Jack Reacher' series, featuring a formidable former military police officer.

name: Bram Stoker
biography: An Irish author, best known today for his 1897 Gothic horror novel 'Dracula,' which introduced the iconic vampire count and has defined the genre for over a century.

name: Shirley Jackson
biography: An American writer known for her horror and mystery works. Her novel 'The Haunting of Hill House' is a classic of the haunted house genre, and her short story 'The Lottery' is a chilling masterpiece.

name: Dan Brown
biography: An American author best known for his thriller novels, including the 'Robert Langdon' series. His novel 'The Da Vinci Code' was a global phenomenon, blending mystery, history, and conspiracy.

name: John Grisham
biography: An American novelist and lawyer, known for his popular legal thrillers. His books, such as 'The Firm' and 'A Time to Kill,' have been adapted into successful films.

name: Georgette Heyer
biography: An English novelist who pioneered the historical romance and Regency romance genres. Her work is celebrated for its meticulous historical detail, witty dialogue, and engaging plots.

name: Beverly Jenkins
biography: A pioneering American author of African-American historical romance. Her work has been instrumental in diversifying the romance genre and has earned her numerous awards.

name: Ken Follett
biography: A Welsh author of thrillers and historical novels. He is best known for his epic historical work 'The Pillars of the Earth' and its sequels, set in the fictional town of Kingsbridge.

name: Robert Graves
biography: An English poet, classical scholar, and novelist. He is best known for his historical novel 'I, Claudius' and his work on Greek mythology, 'The Greek Myths'.

name: Nnedi Okorafor
biography: A Nigerian-American writer of fantasy and science fiction. Her work, which she describes as 'Africanfuturism,' includes the novella 'Binti' and the novel 'Who Fears Death'.

name: Marjane Satrapi
biography: An Iranian-born French graphic novelist and filmmaker. Her graphic memoir 'Persepolis' chronicles her childhood in Iran during and after the Islamic Revolution, receiving global acclaim.

name: Frank McCourt
biography: An Irish-American teacher and writer. He won a Pulitzer Prize for his memoir, 'Angela's Ashes,' which details his impoverished childhood in Limerick, Ireland.

name: Elie Wiesel
biography: A Romanian-born American writer, professor, and Holocaust survivor. His memoir 'Night' is a powerful and harrowing account of his experiences in Nazi concentration camps. He was awarded the Nobel Peace Prize.

name: Malala Yousafzai
biography: A Pakistani activist for female education and the youngest Nobel Prize laureate. Her memoir, 'I Am Malala,' details her fight for education and her survival after being targeted by the Taliban.

name: Howard Zinn
biography: An American historian and social activist. His book 'A People's History of the United States' presented American history from the perspective of marginalized peoples and became a landmark text.

name: Stephen E. Ambrose
biography: An American historian and biographer. He is known for his popular works on American military history, including 'Band of Brothers,' which was adapted into a celebrated HBO miniseries.

name: Nigella Lawson
biography: An English food writer and television cook. Her books, such as 'How to Be a Domestic Goddess,' are known for their conversational, engaging style and focus on comfort and pleasure in cooking.

name: Mark Bittman
biography: An American food journalist and author. His minimalist cookbook, 'How to Cook Everything,' is a modern classic, and his work often advocates for a more sustainable and plant-forward way of eating.

name: Elizabeth Gilbert
biography: An American author, best known for her 2006 memoir, 'Eat, Pray, Love,' which chronicled her journey of self-discovery across Italy, India, and Indonesia after a difficult divorce.

name: Cheryl Strayed
biography: An American memoirist and novelist. Her 2012 memoir, 'Wild: From Lost to Found on the Pacific Crest Trail,' became a bestseller and was adapted into a film. She also wrote the advice column 'Dear Sugar'.

name: Denis Diderot
biography: A French philosopher and writer during the Enlightenment. He was a prominent figure as co-founder and chief editor of the 'Encyclopédie,' a seminal work of the era.

name: Voltaire
biography: A French Enlightenment writer, historian, and philosopher famous for his wit and his advocacy of freedom of speech and religion. His satirical novella 'Candide' is his best-known work.

name: Jean-Jacques Rousseau
biography: A Genevan philosopher and writer whose political philosophy influenced the progress of the Enlightenment. His 'Discourse on Inequality' and 'The Social Contract' are cornerstones of modern political thought.

name: Friedrich Nietzsche
biography: A German philosopher and cultural critic. His work has exerted a profound influence on modern intellectual history, with key ideas including the 'Übermensch' and the 'will to power'.

name: Immanuel Kant
biography: A German philosopher and a central figure in modern philosophy. His work in metaphysics, ethics, and aesthetics, such as 'Critique of Pure Reason,' has had a major influence on subsequent philosophy.

name: René Descartes
biography: A French philosopher, mathematician, and scientist, dubbed the 'father of modern philosophy.' He is famous for his statement 'Cogito, ergo sum' ('I think, therefore I am').

name: Jean-Paul Sartre
biography: A French philosopher, playwright, and political activist. He was one of the key figures in the philosophy of existentialism. His works include 'Being and Nothingness' and the play 'No Exit'.

name: Kathy Sierra
biography: An American programming instructor and game developer. She is the creator of the 'Head First' series of books, which use a visually rich, brain-friendly format to teach technical topics.

name: Erich Gamma
biography: A Swiss computer scientist and one of the four co-authors (the 'Gang of Four') of the influential computer science textbook, 'Design Patterns: Elements of Reusable Object-Oriented Software'.

name: Andrew Hunt
biography: An American author of books on software development. He co-authored the influential book 'The Pragmatic Programmer,' which offers practical advice for software engineers.

name: Sam Newman
biography: A British software developer and author, known for his expertise in microservices architecture. His book 'Building Microservices' is a standard text on the subject in cloud technology.

name: Adrian Cockcroft
biography: A British software engineer who was a key figure in developing cloud systems at Netflix. His talks and writings have been highly influential in the fields of cloud computing and DevOps.

name: Alan Richardson
biography: A software testing consultant and author, known in the automation testing community for his books like 'Selenium Guidebook' and his pragmatic approach to test automation.

name: Stuart Russell
biography: A British computer scientist known for his contributions to artificial intelligence. He co-authored the standard textbook 'Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach' with Peter Norvig.

name: Ian Goodfellow
biography: An American researcher in machine learning, best known for inventing generative adversarial networks (GANs). He is a lead author of the textbook 'Deep Learning'.

name: Trevor Hastie
biography: A statistician and computer scientist at Stanford University. He, along with Tibshirani and Friedman, co-authored 'The Elements of Statistical Learning,' a foundational text in machine learning.

name: Peter Norvig
biography: An American computer scientist and Director of Research at Google. He is the co-author of 'Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach,' the leading university textbook in the field.

name: Douglas R. Hofstadter
biography: An American scholar of cognitive science and author. His 1979 book 'Gödel, Escher, Bach: an Eternal Golden Braid' won the Pulitzer Prize for its exploration of mathematics, symmetry, and intelligence.

name: James Gleick
biography: An American author and journalist. His books explore the cultural implications of science and technology. His 1987 book 'Chaos: Making a New Science' was a bestseller.

name: Linus Pauling
biography: An American chemist and biochemist. He is one of only four individuals to have won two Nobel Prizes. His textbook 'The Nature of the Chemical Bond' was highly influential.

name: Primo Levi
biography: An Italian Jewish chemist, writer, and Holocaust survivor. He is the author of several books, including 'If This Is a Man,' which describes his arrest and incarceration in Auschwitz.

name: Oliver Sacks
biography: A British neurologist and author. His books, such as 'The Man Who Mistook His Wife for a Hat,' explore the human side of neurological disorders through compelling case histories.

name: Simon Singh
biography: A British popular science author and journalist. His books, including 'Fermat's Enigma' and 'The Code Book,' make complex topics in mathematics and cryptography accessible to a general audience.

name: Siddhartha Mukherjee
biography: An Indian-American physician and author. He won the 2011 Pulitzer Prize for General Non-Fiction for his book 'The Emperor of All Maladies: A Biography of Cancer'.

name: Atul Gawande
biography: An American surgeon, writer, and public health researcher. His books, including 'Being Mortal: Medicine and What Matters in the End,' explore the complexities and ethics of modern medicine.

name: Alexander Hamilton
biography: A Founding Father of the United States. Along with James Madison and John Jay, he was a primary author of 'The Federalist Papers,' a collection of essays arguing for the ratification of the US Constitution.

name: Sunil Khilnani
biography: An Indian historian and professor of politics. His book 'The Idea of India' is a widely cited analysis of the political and social history of India since independence.

name: Ramachandra Guha
biography: An Indian historian and writer. His works cover a wide range of topics including environmental, social, and political history. His book 'India After Gandhi' is a monumental work.

name: William Dalrymple
biography: A Scottish historian and writer based in India. His books, such as 'White Mughals' and 'The Last Mughal,' are celebrated for their narrative style and deep research into the history of India.

name: Audrey Truschke
biography: An American historian of South Asia, focusing on the Mughal period. Her writings, including a biography of Aurangzeb, often challenge popular nationalist narratives in India.

name: Romila Thapar
biography: A prominent Indian historian whose principal area of study is ancient India. She is known for her scholarly works that have shaped the historiography of the period.

name: Gurcharan Das
biography: An Indian author and commentator. His works, including 'India Unbound' and 'The Difficulty of Being Good,' explore the economic and moral history of modern India.

name: B. R. Ambedkar
biography: An Indian jurist, economist, and social reformer who was the principal architect of the Constitution of India. His work 'Annihilation of Caste' is a seminal text on the Indian caste system.

name: Jawaharlal Nehru
biography: The first Prime Minister of India. He was also a prolific writer, known for his books 'The Discovery of India' and 'Glimpses of World History,' written during his time in prison.

name: Mahatma Gandhi
biography: Leader of the Indian independence movement. His autobiography, 'The Story of My Experiments with Truth,' is a major work detailing his early life and development of his philosophy of nonviolence.

name: Amartya Sen
biography: An Indian economist and philosopher who was awarded the Nobel Prize in Economic Sciences. His writings, including 'The Argumentative Indian,' have influenced development economics and social choice theory.

name: Raghuram Rajan
biography: An Indian economist and former Governor of the Reserve Bank of India. His books, such as 'Fault Lines' and 'The Third Pillar,' offer insights into global economics and financial crises.

name: Benjamin Graham
biography: A British-born American economist and investor, known as the 'father of value investing.' His books 'The Intelligent Investor' and 'Security Analysis' are foundational texts for investors.

name: Burton Malkiel
biography: An American economist and writer, best known for his classic finance book 'A Random Walk Down Wall Street,' which popularized the random walk hypothesis.

name: John C. Bogle
biography: An American investor and founder of The Vanguard Group. He is credited with creating the first index fund and advocated for low-cost investing in his book 'The Little Book of Common Sense Investing'.

name: Peter Lynch
biography: An American investor and fund manager. He managed the Magellan Fund at Fidelity and achieved massive returns. He authored 'One Up On Wall Street,' offering investment advice to average people.

name: George S. Clason
biography: An American author best known for his book 'The Richest Man in Babylon.' Published in 1926, its parables on thrift and financial planning have made it a personal finance classic.

name: Napoleon Hill
biography: An American self-help author. He is best known for his book 'Think and Grow Rich,' published in 1937, which is one of the all-time bestsellers in the genre.

name: Tim Ferriss
biography: An American entrepreneur, investor, and author. His book 'The 4-Hour Workweek' was a bestseller, and his work focuses on lifestyle design and personal productivity.

name: Ryan Holiday
biography: An American author and marketer. His work focuses on Stoic philosophy and its application to modern life, with popular books like 'The Obstacle Is the Way' and 'Ego Is the Enemy'.

name: Mark Manson
biography: An American self-help author and blogger. His book 'The Subtle Art of Not Giving a F*ck' became a global bestseller for its counterintuitive approach to happiness and self-improvement.

name: Gretchen Rubin
biography: An American author and speaker on the subjects of habits, happiness, and human nature. Her bestselling books include 'The Happiness Project' and 'Better Than Before'.

name: Cal Newport
biography: An American computer science professor and author. His books, such as 'Deep Work' and 'Digital Minimalism,' provide strategies for focused success in a distracted world.

name: Thich Nhat Hanh
biography: A Vietnamese Thiền Buddhist monk, peace activist, and author. A global spiritual leader, his books, like 'The Miracle of Mindfulness,' have been instrumental in bringing mindfulness to the West.

name: Don Miguel Ruiz
biography: A Mexican author of Toltec spiritualist and neoshamanistic texts. His book 'The Four Agreements' presents a simple code of conduct to achieve personal freedom and happiness.

name: Ann Rule
biography: An American author of true crime books. A former police officer, her book 'The Stranger Beside Me,' about the serial killer Ted Bundy whom she knew personally, is a classic of the genre.

name: Michelle McNamara
biography: An American true crime author. Her book 'I'll Be Gone in the Dark,' a detailed investigation into the Golden State Killer, was published posthumously and brought new attention to the case.

name: John E. Douglas
biography: A retired FBI agent and one of the first criminal profilers. His book 'Mindhunter: Inside the FBI's Elite Serial Crime Unit' details the development of psychological profiling to catch serial killers.

name: David Grann
biography: An American journalist and author. He is known for his narrative non-fiction books, including 'The Lost City of Z' and 'Killers of the Flower Moon'.

name: Rebecca Skloot
biography: An American science writer. Her book 'The Immortal Life of Henrietta Lacks' is a work of narrative non-fiction that investigates the story of the woman whose cancer cells became the first immortal human cell line.

name: George R. R. R. Martin
biography: Duplicate of George R.R. Martin. Replacing with another author: C.S. Lewis.

name: C.S. Lewis
biography: A British writer and lay theologian. He is best known for 'The Chronicles of Narnia' fantasy series and for his works of Christian apologetics, such as 'Mere Christianity'.

name: Lewis Carroll
biography: The pen name of Charles Lutwidge Dodgson, an English writer. His most famous writings are 'Alice's Adventures in Wonderland' and its sequel 'Through the Looking-Glass'.

name: Roald Dahl
biography: A British novelist, short-story writer, and poet. His books, known for their dark humor and imaginative plots, include classics like 'Charlie and the Chocolate Factory' and 'Matilda'.

name: A.A. Milne
biography: An English author, best known for his books about the teddy bear 'Winnie-the-Pooh' and for various poems. His works are beloved classics of children's literature.

name: L.M. Montgomery
biography: A Canadian author best known for a series of novels beginning in 1908 with 'Anne of Green Gables.' The book was an immediate success and has been cherished for generations.

name: Louisa May Alcott
biography: An American novelist and poet best known as the author of the novel 'Little Women' and its sequels. The book is a semi-autobiographical account of her childhood.

name: Madeleine L'Engle
biography: An American writer best known for her young adult fiction. Her work 'A Wrinkle in Time' won the Newbery Medal and is a classic of the science fantasy genre.

name: Rick Riordan
biography: An American author. He is known for writing the 'Percy Jackson & the Olympians' series, which blends Greek mythology with modern-day adventure.

name: Eoin Colfer
biography: An Irish author of children's books. He is best known for being the author of the 'Artemis Fowl' series, which follows a teenage criminal mastermind.

name: Philip Pullman
biography: An English author of several bestselling books, most notably the fantasy trilogy 'His Dark Materials,' which serves as a reimagining of Milton's 'Paradise Lost'.

name: Dr. Seuss
biography: The pen name of Theodor Seuss Geisel, an American children's author and cartoonist. He is known for his imaginative characters, rhyme, and meter in books like 'The Cat in the Hat'.

name: Shel Silverstein
biography: An American writer, poet, and cartoonist. He was the author of iconic books of children's poetry, including 'Where the Sidewalk Ends' and 'A Light in the Attic'.

name: Maurice Sendak
biography: An American illustrator and writer of children's books. He was best known for his book 'Where the Wild Things Are,' a classic celebrated for its honest portrayal of childhood emotions.

name: Sarat Chandra Chattopadhyay
biography: A leading Bengali novelist and short story writer of the early 20th century. His works, such as 'Devdas' and 'Parineeta', are celebrated for their sensitive portrayal of women and social customs.

name: Bibhutibhushan Bandyopadhyay
biography: An Indian writer in the Bengali language. He is best known for his autobiographical novel, 'Pather Panchali' (The Song of the Road), which was adapted into Satyajit Ray's acclaimed Apu Trilogy.

name: Jibanananda Das
biography: A major poet of modern Bengali literature. His poetry, noted for its surreal imagery and exploration of nature and existential themes, gained widespread recognition after his death. Wrote 'Banalata Sen'.

name: Mirza Ghalib
biography: A preeminent Urdu and Persian poet during the late Mughal Empire. He is one of the most popular and influential poets of the Urdu language, celebrated for his ghazals.

name: Faiz Ahmed Faiz
biography: A revolutionary Pakistani poet and a prominent member of the Progressive Writers' Movement. His work is known for its blend of classical Urdu forms with modern, socialist themes.

name: P. L. Deshpande
biography: A beloved Marathi writer and humorist, affectionately known as 'Pu La'. A multifaceted talent, he was a writer, musician, and orator whose humorous works have been cherished for generations.

name: Vijay Tendulkar
biography: A leading Indian playwright, screenwriter, and political journalist. His plays, such as 'Shantata! Court Chalu Aahe' and 'Ghashiram Kotwal', offered a powerful critique of social and political issues.

name: K. M. Munshi
biography: An Indian independence activist, politician, and writer. He was a prolific author of historical fiction in Gujarati, including his famous 'Patan' trilogy. He also founded the Bharatiya Vidya Bhavan.

name: Gopinath Mohanty
biography: A celebrated Odia novelist and a Jnanpith Award recipient. His works, such as 'Paraja' and 'Mati Matala', realistically depict the lives of tribal communities and rural society in Odisha.

name: Birendra Kumar Bhattacharya
biography: An Assamese novelist and the first writer from Assam to win the Jnanpith Award. His novel 'Mrityunjay' is a classic, set against the backdrop of the Quit India Movement of 1942.

name: Julio Cortázar
biography: An Argentine novelist and short story writer. A master of the fantastic, his works, including the experimental novel 'Hopscotch,' had a profound influence on the Latin American Boom.

name: Mario Vargas Llosa
biography: A Peruvian novelist and Nobel laureate. A leading figure of the Latin American Boom, his works, like 'The Time of the Hero' and 'The Feast of the Goat', often explore power and politics.

name: Carlos Fuentes
biography: A Mexican novelist and essayist. Among the most admired writers in the Spanish-speaking world, his works, including 'The Death of Artemio Cruz,' explore Mexican identity and history.

name: Roberto Bolaño
biography: A Chilean novelist and poet. He gained posthumous international fame for his novels 'The Savage Detectives' and '2666,' which are celebrated for their sprawling scope and literary ambition.

name: José Saramago
biography: A Portuguese writer and Nobel laureate. His novels, such as 'Blindness' and 'The Gospel According to Jesus Christ,' are known for their allegorical themes and unique punctuation style.

name: Nikolai Gogol
biography: A Russian novelist and playwright of Ukrainian origin. He is considered a father of modern Russian realism. His works include the novel 'Dead Souls' and the short story 'The Overcoat'.

name: Ivan Turgenev
biography: A major Russian novelist and playwright. His novel 'Fathers and Sons' is a classic of 19th-century fiction. He was a contemporary of Tolstoy and Dostoevsky.

name: Mikhail Bulgakov
biography: A Russian writer, physician, and playwright. His novel 'The Master and Margarita,' a dark, satirical fantasy, is considered one of the masterpieces of 20th-century literature.

name: Henrik Ibsen
biography: A Norwegian playwright and theatre director. As one of the founders of modernism in theatre, he is often referred to as 'the father of realism'. Known for plays like 'A Doll's House'.

name: August Strindberg
biography: A Swedish playwright, novelist, and painter. A prolific writer, his plays, such as 'Miss Julie,' were known for their psychological realism and naturalism.

name: Émile Zola
biography: A French novelist and playwright. He was a major figure in the literary school of naturalism and a key contributor to the development of theatrical naturalism. Known for his open letter 'J'Accuse…!'.

name: Stendhal
biography: The pen name of Marie-Henri Beyle, a 19th-century French writer. He is known for the psychological depth of his characters in novels like 'The Red and the Black' and 'The Charterhouse of Parma'.

name: Czesław Miłosz
biography: A Polish-American poet, prose writer, and Nobel laureate. His work, including 'The Captive Mind,' explores themes of politics, history, and moral responsibility in 20th-century Europe.

name: Charles Darwin
biography: English naturalist, geologist and biologist. He is celebrated for his contributions to the science of evolution. His 1859 book 'On the Origin of Species' is a foundational text of modern biology.

name: Richard Dawkins
biography: An English ethologist and evolutionary biologist. His 1976 book 'The Selfish Gene' popularized the gene-centered view of evolution. He is also a prominent atheist and author.

name: E. O. Wilson
biography: An American biologist, naturalist, and writer. His work on sociobiology and biodiversity earned him the title 'the father of sociobiology'. He was a two-time winner of the Pulitzer Prize.

name: Antoine Lavoisier
biography: A French nobleman and chemist central to the 18th-century chemical revolution. He is considered the 'father of modern chemistry' for his work on combustion and stoichiometry.

name: Peter Drucker
biography: An Austrian-American management consultant and author. His books and scholarly articles explored how humans are organized across business and government. Hailed as the founder of modern management.

name: Daniel Goleman
biography: An American author and science journalist. For twelve years, he wrote for The New York Times, reporting on the brain and behavioral sciences. His book 'Emotional Intelligence' was a global bestseller.

name: Michael Lewis
biography: An American author and financial journalist. His bestselling books include 'Liar's Poker,' 'The Big Short,' and 'Moneyball,' known for their accessible and narrative-driven explanations of complex topics.

name: Guido van Rossum
biography: A Dutch programmer best known as the creator of the Python programming language, for which he was the 'Benevolent Dictator for Life' (BDFL) until he stepped down in 2018.

name: Yukihiro Matsumoto (Matz)
biography: A Japanese computer scientist and software programmer best known as the chief designer of the Ruby programming language and its reference implementation, Matz's Ruby Interpreter (MRI).

name: Gene Kim
biography: An American author and researcher. He is a prominent figure in the DevOps movement and is best known for his books 'The Phoenix Project' and 'The Unicorn Project'.

name: Martin Gardner
biography: An American popular mathematics and science writer. For many years, he wrote the 'Mathematical Games' column for Scientific American, which introduced recreational mathematics to a wide audience.

name: Benoît Mandelbrot
biography: A Polish-born French-American mathematician. Recognized for his work on fractal geometry, he coined the term 'fractal' and developed the theory of 'roughness' in the real world.

name: Jim Butcher
biography: An American author best known for his contemporary fantasy book series 'The Dresden Files,' which follows a private investigator and wizard in modern-day Chicago.

name: Charlaine Harris
biography: An American author who has been writing mysteries for over thirty years. She is best known for 'The Southern Vampire Mysteries' series, which was adapted into the TV show 'True Blood'.

name: Leigh Bardugo
biography: An Israeli-American fantasy author. She is best known for her 'Grishaverse' novels, which include the 'Shadow and Bone' trilogy and the 'Six of Crows' duology.

name: Cassandra Clare
biography: The pen name of Judith Lewis, an American author of young adult fiction. She is best known for her bestselling series 'The Mortal Instruments'.

name: William Gibson
biography: An American-Canadian speculative fiction writer credited with pioneering the science fiction subgenre of cyberpunk. He coined the term 'cyberspace' in his short story 'Burning Chrome'.

name: Andy Weir
biography: An American novelist and software engineer. He is best known for his debut novel, 'The Martian,' a work of hard science fiction that was adapted into a successful film.

name: Ann Leckie
biography: An American author of science fiction and fantasy. Her debut novel 'Ancillary Justice' won the Hugo Award, Nebula Award, and Arthur C. Clarke Award, a rare triple crown.

name: Anne Rice
biography: An American author of gothic fiction, Christian literature, and erotica. She was best known for her series of novels, 'The Vampire Chronicles,' which revolves around the central character Lestat.

name: Peter Straub
biography: An American novelist and poet. He was known for his horror and supernatural fiction, including 'Ghost Story' and his collaboration with Stephen King, 'The Talisman'.

name: Lisa Kleypas
