biography: An Italian philosopher, poet, and philologist. He is considered one of the greatest Italian poets of the 19th century and a leading figure of literary Romanticism.

name: Chitra Mudgal
biography: A distinguished contemporary Hindi writer. Her novel 'Avaan,' dealing with the trade union movement, is highly acclaimed. She was awarded the Vyas Samman for her work.

name: Nasira Sharma
biography: A Hindi novelist and journalist. Her works often draw from her experiences in Iran and deal with themes of cultural conflict and women's issues. She won the Sahitya Akademi Award for her novel 'Parijat'.

name: Gyan Chaturvedi
biography: A leading satirist in contemporary Hindi literature. A cardiologist by profession, his satirical novels like 'Baramasi' offer a humorous critique of the Indian medical system and society.

name: Mamta Kalia
biography: A prominent Indian author, poet, and playwright in Hindi. Her works often focus on the urban middle-class experience. She won the Vyas Samman for her novel 'Dukkham Sukkham'.

name: Kashinath Singh
biography: A distinguished Hindi writer known for his unique portrayal of life in Benares (Varanasi). His novel 'Kashi Ka Assi' is a modern classic. A recipient of the Sahitya Akademi Award.

name: Manik Bandopadhyay
biography: A major Bengali novelist and a key figure in modern Bengali literature. His novels 'Padma Nadir Majhi' and 'Putul Nacher Itikatha' are classics, known for their realism and psychological depth.

name: Shirshendu Mukhopadhyay
biography: A popular Bengali author. He has written in various genres, including adult fiction, thrillers, and children's literature, creating the beloved detective character Shabar Dasgupta.

name: Manto
biography: Duplicate of Saadat Hasan Manto. Replacing with another author: Rajinder Singh Bedi.

name: Rajinder Singh Bedi
biography: An eminent Urdu writer and a leading figure of the Progressive Writers' Movement. He is known for his realistic and sensitive short stories, such as 'Lajwanti,' and for his film work.

name: Vinda Karandikar
biography: A Marathi poet, writer, and a Jnanpith Award recipient. His work includes modernist poetry, essays, and acclaimed translations of Aristotle and Shakespeare.

name: Iravati Karve
biography: An Indian sociologist, anthropologist, and writer. Her book 'Yuganta: The End of an Epoch' offers a brilliant anthropological analysis of the characters and events of the Mahabharata.

name: Umashankar Joshi
biography: A poet, scholar, and writer who was a recipient of the Jnanpith Award. His works, including 'Nishith' and 'Visamo', made a significant contribution to Gujarati literature.

name: Chandrakant Bakshi
biography: A popular and prolific Gujarati writer. He was known for his distinctive, aggressive writing style and for his novels and short stories that often explored urban themes and existentialism.

name: Manoj Das
biography: A bilingual writer who wrote in Odia and English. He was a master of the short story form, known for his simple, witty, and often mystical tales. A recipient of the Padma Bhushan.

name: Hiren Bhattacharyya
biography: A popular Assamese poet, known as 'Hiru Da'. He is celebrated for his lyrical and romantic poetry, which often deals with themes of love, nature, and humanity.

name: Thiruvalluvar
biography: Celebrated ancient Tamil poet and philosopher, author of the Tirukkural, a timeless ethical masterpiece comprising 1330 couplets on virtue, wealth, and love, revered for its universal wisdom.

name: Ilango Adigal
biography: A Jain prince and poet, traditionally credited with authoring 'Silappathikaram' (The Tale of an Anklet), one of the Five Great Epics of Tamil Literature.

name: Kamban
biography: A medieval Tamil poet and the author of the 'Ramavataram', the popular Tamil version of the Ramayana. His work is celebrated for its poetic excellence and profound character development.

name: Kannadasan
biography: A prolific Tamil poet and lyricist. Renowned for his philosophical and romantic film songs, he also wrote novels, essays, and his famous autobiography 'Vanavasam'.

name: Bharathidasan
biography: A 20th-century poet and rationalist writer. A follower of Subramania Bharati, his works championed the Dravidian Movement, social reform, and the beauty of the Tamil language.

name: Viswanatha Satyanarayana
biography: A towering figure in 20th-century Telugu literature, honored with the Jnanpith Award. A poet, novelist, and scholar, his magnum opus is the epic 'Ramayana Kalpavruksham'.

name: C. Narayana Reddy
biography: A prolific poet, lyricist, and academic, popularly known as 'CiNaRe'. He received the Jnanpith Award for his poetic work 'Viswambhara' and wrote thousands of popular film songs.

name: Chalam (Gudipati Venkatachalam)
biography: A rebellious and controversial writer who championed women's liberation and sexual freedom. His novels, like 'Maidanam,' challenged the patriarchal norms of his time.

name: Girish Karnad
biography: An acclaimed playwright, actor, and film director. His plays, such as 'Tughlaq' and 'Hayavadana,' blend history, myth, and folk traditions with modern sensibilities. A Jnanpith Award winner.

name: S. L. Bhyrappa
biography: A highly popular and bestselling Kannada novelist. His works, including 'Parva' and 'Aavarana,' are known for their philosophical depth and exploration of Indian history, culture, and values.

name: D. R. Bendre
biography: A renowned Kannada poet and a prominent figure of the 'Navodaya' period. Known by the pen name 'Ambikatanayadatta', he won the Jnanpith Award for his poetry collection 'Naaku Tanti'.

name: Shivaram Karanth
biography: A major novelist, playwright, and environmentalist. A Jnanpith Award winner, his novels like 'Marali Mannige' and 'Mookajjiya Kanasugalu' are classics.

name: Thakazhi Sivasankara Pillai
biography: A novelist and short story writer who pioneered realism in Malayalam literature. His epic novel 'Chemmeen' won the Sahitya Akademi Award. A recipient of the Jnanpith Award.

name: O. V. Vijayan
biography: A novelist and short story writer. His debut novel, 'Khasakkinte Ithihasam' (The Legends of Khasak), is a landmark work of modernist literature in Malayalam.

name: S. K. Pottekkatt
biography: A renowned travelogue writer and novelist. He won the Jnanpith Award for his novel 'Oru Desathinte Katha'. His vivid travelogues brought the world to Malayalam readers.

name: Plutarch
biography: A Greek biographer and essayist. He is known for his 'Parallel Lives,' a series of biographies of famous Greeks and Romans, and 'Moralia,' a collection of essays and speeches.

name: Livy
biography: A Roman historian. He wrote a monumental history of Rome and the Roman people, 'Ab Urbe Condita,' covering the period from the earliest legends of Rome before the traditional foundation in 753 BC.

name: Montaigne
biography: One of the most significant philosophers of the French Renaissance, known for popularizing the essay as a literary genre. His work 'Essais' contains some of the most influential essays ever written.

name: Baruch Spinoza
biography: A Dutch philosopher of Portuguese Sephardi origin. A leading figure of the Enlightenment, his magnum opus, 'Ethics,' is a masterpiece of rationalist philosophy.

name: John Locke
biography: An English philosopher and physician, widely regarded as one of the most influential of Enlightenment thinkers and commonly known as the 'Father of Liberalism'.

name: David Hume
biography: A Scottish Enlightenment philosopher, historian, and economist. He is best known for his highly influential system of philosophical empiricism, skepticism, and naturalism.

name: Ludwig Wittgenstein
biography: An Austrian-British philosopher who worked primarily in logic and the philosophy of language. His 'Tractatus Logico-Philosophicus' and 'Philosophical Investigations' are major 20th-century works.

name: Martin Heidegger
biography: A German philosopher and a seminal figure in the Continental tradition of philosophy. He is best known for his work 'Being and Time,' a foundational text of existentialism.

name: Erving Goffman
biography: A Canadian-American sociologist and writer. He is known for his work on social interaction and the 'dramaturgical approach,' as detailed in his book 'The Presentation of Self in Everyday Life'.

name: Pierre Bourdieu
biography: A French sociologist and anthropologist. His work, such as 'Distinction: A Social Critique of the Judgement of Taste,' explored the dynamics of power in society.

name: Clifford Geertz
biography: An American anthropologist who is remembered mostly for his strong support for and influence on the practice of symbolic anthropology. Known for his essay 'Deep Play: Notes on the Balinese Cockfight'.

name: B.F. Skinner
biography: An American psychologist and behaviorist. He developed the theory of operant conditioning – the idea that behavior is determined by its consequences. A pioneer of modern behaviorism.

name: Carl Rogers
biography: An American psychologist and among the founders of the humanistic approach to psychology. He is widely considered to be one of the founding fathers of psychotherapy research.

name: Milgram
biography: This is a surname only. Replacing with another author: Stanley Milgram.

name: Stanley Milgram
biography: An American social psychologist, best known for his controversial experiment on obedience to authority figures, the 'Milgram experiment,' conducted in the 1960s.

name: Philip Zimbardo
biography: An American psychologist and a professor emeritus at Stanford University. He became known for his 1971 Stanford prison experiment and has authored various introductory psychology books.

name: Richard Thaler
biography: An American economist and Nobel laureate. A theorist in behavioral economics, he co-authored the global bestseller 'Nudge,' which explores how public and private organizations can help people make better choices.

name: George Akerlof
biography: An American economist and Nobel laureate. His 1970 paper, 'The Market for Lemons,' is a foundational text on the role of asymmetric information in markets.

name: E. H. Gombrich
biography: An Austrian-born art historian who became a naturalised British citizen. His book 'The Story of Art' is one of the most accessible and popular introductions to the visual arts ever written.

name: John Berger
biography: An English art critic, novelist, and painter. His 1972 book and BBC series 'Ways of Seeing' revolutionized the way art is understood, particularly in relation to ideology and gender.

name: Linda Nochlin
biography: An American art historian and a leading figure in feminist art history. Her 1971 essay, 'Why Have There Been No Great Women Artists?', is a foundational text of the field.

name: Robert Hughes
biography: An Australian-born art critic and writer. He was the art critic for Time magazine for over 30 years. His book and TV series 'The Shock of the New' surveyed modern art.

name: Alex Ross
biography: An American music critic. He has been a staff writer for The New Yorker since 1996. His 2007 book, 'The Rest Is Noise: Listening to the Twentieth Century,' was a Pulitzer Prize finalist.

name: Charles Rosen
biography: An American pianist and writer on music. He is remembered for his scholarly and eloquent books, including 'The Classical Style,' an analysis of the music of Haydn, Mozart, and Beethoven.

name: Pauline Kael
biography: An American film critic who wrote for The New Yorker magazine from 1968 to 1991. She was known for her witty, pugnacious, and highly opinionated reviews.

name: Roger Ebert
biography: An American film critic and historian. He was the first film critic to win the Pulitzer Prize for Criticism. His reviews were syndicated to newspapers nationwide.

name: François Truffaut
biography: A French film director and a founder of the French New Wave. His book-length interview 'Hitchcock/Truffaut' is a classic text on film direction and analysis.

name: Vitruvius
biography: A Roman author, architect, and engineer during the 1st century BC. He is the author of 'De architectura,' a treatise on architecture that has been a major influence on Western architecture.

name: Le Corbusier
biography: A Swiss-French architect, designer, and a pioneer of modern architecture. His book 'Towards a New Architecture' was a highly influential manifesto for the modernist movement.

name: Frank Lloyd Wright
biography: An American architect, designer, and writer. He designed more than 1,000 structures over a creative period of 70 years and was a leader of the Prairie School movement of architecture.

name: Rem Koolhaas
biography: A Dutch architect, architectural theorist, and urbanist. His 1978 book, 'Delirious New York: A Retroactive Manifesto for Manhattan,' is a classic text of modern architectural theory.

name: Jane Jacobs
biography: An American-Canadian journalist and activist. Her influential book 'The Death and Life of Great American Cities' critiqued urban renewal policies and championed vibrant, mixed-use neighborhoods.

name: Lewis Mumford
biography: An American historian and sociologist noted for his writing on cities and urban architecture. His book 'The City in History' won the National Book Award.

name: Christopher Alexander
biography: A British-American architect and design theorist. He is the author of the influential books 'A Pattern Language' and 'The Timeless Way of Building'.

name: John Ruskin
biography: A leading English art critic of the Victorian era, as well as an art patron, draughtsman, and watercolourist. He wrote on subjects ranging from geology to architecture and political economy.

name: J.G. Farrell
biography: A British novelist of Irish descent. He gained prominence for his historical fiction, most notably his 'Empire Trilogy' ('Troubles', 'The Siege of Krishnapur', and 'The Singapore Grip').

name: John Fowles
biography: An English novelist of international stature, critically positioned between modernism and postmodernism. His works include 'The Collector,' 'The Magus,' and 'The French Lieutenant's Woman'.

name: Muriel Spark
biography: A Scottish novelist, short story writer, and poet. Her 1961 novel 'The Prime of Miss Jean Brodie' is her most famous work and a modern classic.

name: Iris Murdoch
biography: An Irish and British novelist and philosopher. Her novels, such as 'The Sea, the Sea' (which won the Booker Prize), are known for their exploration of morality, good, and evil.

name: Angela Carter
biography: An English novelist, short story writer, and journalist. Her work, including 'The Bloody Chamber' and 'Nights at the Circus,' is known for its feminism, magical realism, and picaresque style.

name: William Golding
biography: A British novelist and Nobel laureate. He is best known for his debut novel 'Lord of the Flies,' an allegorical tale about a group of British boys stranded on an uninhabited island.

name: Kingsley Amis
biography: An English novelist, poet, and critic. He is best known for his satirical comic novels, such as 'Lucky Jim,' which captured the mood of post-war Britain.

name: George MacDonald
biography: A Scottish author, poet, and Christian minister. He was a pioneering figure in the field of modern fantasy literature. His works, such as 'Phantastes,' influenced C.S. Lewis and J.R.R. Tolkien.

name: Lord Dunsany
biography: An Anglo-Irish writer and dramatist. A prolific author, he is considered a key figure in the development of the fantasy genre, influencing Tolkien, Lovecraft, and many others.

name: M. R. James
biography: An English author and medievalist scholar. He is best known for his ghost stories, which are considered among the finest in the genre. He redefined the ghost story for the 20th century.

name: Algernon Blackwood
biography: An English short story writer and novelist, one of the most prolific writers of ghost stories in the history of the genre. 'The Willows' is one of his most famous tales.

name: Ramsey Campbell
biography: An English horror fiction writer. He is considered one of the great living masters of horror literature. His work is known for its psychological depth and subtle dread.

name: Clive Barker
biography: An English playwright, novelist, and film director. He came to prominence in the mid-1980s with a series of short stories, the 'Books of Blood,' which established him as a leading horror writer.

name: Sekkizhar
biography: A 12th-century poet and saint, revered for authoring the 'Periya Puranam,' a hagiography detailing the lives of the 63 Nayanars (Saivite saints). The work is a cornerstone of Tamil Saiva Siddhanta.

name: Pattinathar
biography: A revered ascetic poet, traditionally believed to have lived around the 10th or 14th century. His philosophical poems critique materialism and advocate for renunciation and the search for spiritual truth.

name: Arunagirinathar
biography: A 15th-century Tamil poet. He is the creator of 'Thiruppugazh,' a collection of devotional hymns dedicated to Lord Murugan, celebrated for its intricate rhythms and lyrical beauty.

name: Sivagnana Munivar
biography: An 18th-century Saivite scholar and saint. He is most famous for his extensive and authoritative commentary on the Sivagnana Bodham, known as the 'Sivagnana Bhashyam' or 'Dravida Bhashyam'.

name: Tayumanavar
biography: An 18th-century spiritual philosopher and poet. His works advocate for a synthesis of Advaita Vedanta and Saiva Siddhanta, expressing a universal and inclusive spiritual vision.

name: Ramalinga Adigalar
biography: A 19th-century saint and poet known as Vallalar. He was the founder of the 'Samarasa Suddha Sanmarga' movement. His vast body of work, 'Thiruvarutpa', preaches compassion and universal brotherhood.

name: Mayuram Vedanayagam Pillai
biography: A 19th-century writer, judge, and social reformer. He is credited with writing the first novel in Tamil, 'Prathapa Mudaliar Charithiram' (1879), and advocated for women's education and rights.

name: Pavaloreru Perunchithiranar
biography: A 20th-century poet and a key figure in the 'Thanittamil Iyakkam' (Pure Tamil Movement). His poetry and writings were known for their fierce advocacy of Tamil linguistic and national identity.

name: K. V. Jagannathan (Ki. Va. Ja.)
biography: A scholar and folklorist who served as the editor of the literary magazine 'Kalaimagal'. He travelled extensively to collect and publish Tamil folk songs and stories, winning the Sahitya Akademi Award.

name: Ku. Alagirisami
biography: A major short story writer and literary editor. Influenced by Russian realists, his stories are celebrated for their profound humanism, compassion, and realistic portrayal of the lives of ordinary people.

name: Akilan
biography: A popular novelist and short story writer. He was a recipient of the Jnanpith Award. His novel 'Chittirappavai' won the Sahitya Akademi Award. His works often have a strong social and moral message.

name: Naa. Parthasarathy
biography: A writer and journalist who wrote under the pen name 'Deepam'. His novel 'Samudhaya Veedhi' won the Sahitya Akademi Award. His works, both social and historical, often espoused Gandhian ideals.

name: M. Varadarasan (Mu.Va.)
biography: A scholar and novelist. His novels, like 'Kallo Kaviyamo', were immensely popular and conveyed moral messages in a simple style. He won the Sahitya Akademi Award for 'Agal Vilakku'.

name: Pattukkottai Prabhakar
biography: A highly prolific and popular Tamil author of crime and detective fiction. He has written hundreds of novels and short stories, becoming a household name through weekly magazines.

name: Indra Soundar Rajan
biography: A popular Tamil author known for his supernatural and divine thriller novels, often set against the backdrop of ancient temples and traditions in Tamil Nadu. Many of his works have been adapted for television.

name: B.R. Rajam Aiyar
biography: A pioneer of the Tamil novel. His 1896 work, 'Kamalambal Charitram,' is considered one of the earliest social novels in the language, noted for its realism and psychological depth.

name: Anuthama
biography: A popular female writer of the mid-20th century. Her novels, such as 'Oru Veedu Iru Ullam,' often focused on family values, relationships, and the lives of women in a traditional setting.

name: Pudhiyavan
biography: A contemporary poet and writer, known for his work in both poetry and prose. His writing often reflects a keen observation of social realities and human behavior.

name: Kavingnar Vali
biography: A legendary poet and film lyricist. With a career spanning over five decades, he wrote thousands of songs known for their philosophical depth, playful wit, and profound simplicity, leaving an indelible mark on Tamil cinema.

name: Kothamangalam Seenu
biography: A stage actor and singer of the early 20th century. While not primarily a writer, he contributed to the scripts and songs of the plays he was involved in, influencing the theatrical landscape.

name: Subramania Siva
biography: An Indian freedom fighter and writer. A close associate of Subramania Bharati, he used his powerful oratory and writings in journals like 'Gnana Bhanu' to inspire nationalism and social reform.

name: Kavingnar Tamiloli
biography: A poet and a key figure in the progressive literary movement. Influenced by communist ideology, his poetry powerfully voiced the struggles of the working class and the oppressed.

name: Pa. Jeevanandham
biography: A social reformer and one of the pioneers of the communist movement in Tamil Nadu. A powerful orator and writer, he used his literary skills to propagate socialist and rationalist ideas.

name: S. D. S. Yogi
biography: A poet, writer, and film director. He was associated with the Indian freedom struggle and his works often carried patriotic themes. He translated the works of Omar Khayyam into Tamil.

name: Namakkal Kavignar Ramalingam Pillai
biography: A poet and artist who was the first to be named Poet Laureate of the Tamil Nadu government. His patriotic song 'Kathiyindri Raththamindri' was famously sung during the Salt March.

name: A. S. Gnanasambandan
biography: A distinguished scholar of Tamil literature, particularly known for his insightful comparative studies of Kamban's Ramayana and Shakespeare. He was a respected academic and a captivating orator.

name: P. Sri Acharya
biography: A scholar and writer who specialized in Vaishnavite philosophy and history. He wrote detailed commentaries on the works of the Alvars and other Vaishnava texts, making them more accessible to the public.

name: Karichan Kunju
biography: A writer and translator, known for his novel 'Pasitha Manidam', a significant work that explores themes of hunger and existentialism. He also translated the works of acclaimed Malayalam writer Vaikom Muhammad Basheer into Tamil.

name: T. K. C. (T. K. Chidambaranatha Mudaliar)
biography: A scholar and literary connoisseur, known for his unique approach to literary appreciation, which he termed 'rasanai' (relishing). He was a major influence on the study of Kamban's Ramayana.

name: Lena Tamilvanan
biography: A writer, publisher, and the son of the writer Tamilvanan. He is known for his self-help and motivational books, and for continuing the 'Manimekalai Prasuram' publishing house.

name: Tamilvanan
biography: A writer and publisher who founded 'Manimekalai Prasuram'. He was known for his detective novels featuring the character 'Sankarlal' and for his accessible books on a wide variety of subjects.

name: Ra. Ki. Rangarajan
biography: A journalist and writer who worked for 'Kumudam' magazine. He was a prolific ghostwriter for the popular writer 'Mohan' and also wrote many successful novels and short stories under his own name.

name: A. K. Perumal
biography: A contemporary folklorist and scholar from the Kanyakumari region. He has done extensive fieldwork to document the folk arts, rituals, and history of southern Tamil Nadu, preserving a rich cultural heritage.

name: Vaduvoor Duraiswamy Iyengar
biography: An early pioneer of the detective novel in Tamil literature. His novel 'Menaka' was one of the first to be adapted into a Tamil film. He created the popular detective character 'Digambara Samiar'.

name: J. R. Rangaraju
biography: An early 20th-century novelist, considered one of the pioneers of the social novel in Tamil. His novel 'Rajambal' was a bestseller and dealt with contemporary social issues.

name: M. R. Radha
biography: A legendary stage and screen actor, known as 'Nadigavel'. His powerful, anti-establishment dialogues and his unique acting style made him a counter-cultural icon. His life is a key chapter in Tamil theatre history.

name: Gnani Sankaran
biography: A prominent journalist, theatre personality, and political commentator. He was known for his sharp and critical analysis of politics and society through his columns, plays, and public talks.

name: Kavingnar Inkulab
biography: A revolutionary poet and rationalist writer. His poetry, including the famous 'Naan Manushana Irukken', was a fiery voice against social injustice, caste oppression, and state power.

name: A. S. K. (A. S. Krishnaswami)
biography: A scholar and critic, known for his deep knowledge of both Tamil and English literature. He wrote insightful literary criticism and was respected for his intellectual prowess and balanced judgment.

name: M. Arunachalam
biography: A scholar who undertook the monumental task of documenting the history of Tamil literature century by century. His multi-volume 'Tamil Ilakkiya Varalaru' is an indispensable resource for students and researchers.

name: K. D. Thirunavukkarasu
biography: A scholar and critic, known for his work on ancient Tamil literature and his Marxist interpretation of the Tirukkural. He was a prominent figure in the field of Tamil literary research.

name: K. P. A. Samy
biography: A writer and scholar who has written on a variety of subjects, including history, literature, and religion. His work is known for its research and its aim to educate the general reader.

name: S. M. Kamal
biography: A historian from the Ramanathapuram region. He has written extensively on the history of the Sethupathi kings and the Maravar community, providing valuable historical accounts of the region.

name: N. Sethuraman
biography: A historian and epigraphist. He dedicated his life to the study of temple inscriptions and the history of the Chola and Pandya dynasties, publishing several important research works on the subject.

name: S. Agasthiarlingam
biography: A distinguished linguist and the founder of the Centre for Advanced Study in Linguistics at Annamalai University. He made pioneering contributions to the study of Dravidian linguistics and Tamil grammar.

name: C. Mahalingam (Ilanthendral)
biography: A contemporary poet and writer, known for his lyrical poetry and his contributions to magazines. His work often explores themes of nature, love, and human emotion.

name: Kavingar J. Inok
biography: A contemporary poet known for his Christian devotional poetry. His works blend spiritual themes with modern poetic sensibilities, making him a distinct voice in contemporary religious literature.

name: Thellur Dharmarajan
biography: A contemporary writer and critic. His work is known for its sharp, intellectual, and often provocative analysis of literature, culture, and politics, challenging established viewpoints.

name: Puliyur Kesikan
biography: A scholar who wrote simple and accessible prose commentaries for many classical Tamil texts, including the Sangam literature and the Tirukkural, making them available to a wider audience.

name: P. L. Samy
biography: A scholar who uniquely combined his knowledge of science (zoology) with a study of ancient Tamil literature, writing books that explored the flora and fauna described in Sangam poetry.

name: S. Vaiyapuri Pillai
biography: An influential scholar, lexicographer, and editor. He was the chief editor of the Tamil Lexicon project and his work on dating classical Tamil texts, though controversial, was highly significant.

name: Periyar E. V. Ramasamy
biography: A social activist and politician who started the Self-Respect Movement. His writings, particularly in journals like 'Kudi Arasu,' were powerful polemics against caste, religion, and social superstition.

name: S. Jeyaseela Stephen
biography: A historian specializing in the maritime history of South India and the social history of Christians in the region. His research has shed light on colonial and pre-colonial interactions.

name: A. Sivasubramanian
biography: A prominent folklorist and cultural historian. His work focuses on documenting the histories and cultures of marginalized communities and subaltern groups in Tamil Nadu.

name: K. Rajan
biography: An archaeologist and historian. His archaeological fieldwork, particularly at sites like Kodumanal and Keeladi, and his writings have been crucial in understanding ancient Tamil history.

name: R. Kalaikkovan
biography: A medical doctor and epigraphist. He founded the Dr. M. Rajamanikkanar Centre for Historical Research, which has published numerous valuable studies on temple inscriptions and local history.

name: A. H. A. Hameed
biography: A Sri Lankan Tamil writer and broadcaster. He is a prominent figure in the literary and media scene, known for his short stories, essays, and his work with the BBC Tamil service.

name: M. L. Thangappa
biography: A scholar and translator, known for his acclaimed English translations of Sangam poetry and other classical Tamil works, which have introduced ancient Tamil literature to a global readership.

name: V. I. Subramoniam
biography: A renowned linguist and a pioneer in the field of Dravidian studies. He was the founder-director of the International School of Dravidian Linguistics.

name: Pavarasu
biography: A contemporary poet known for his sharp, satirical, and often humorous take on modern life, politics, and social conventions. His style is direct and accessible.

name: Kalyanaraman (V. Kalyanaraman)
biography: A contemporary writer and translator. He is known for his acclaimed English translations of major contemporary Tamil writers, including Perumal Murugan and Imayam.

name: Sudhangan
biography: A veteran journalist and political analyst. He has written several books on contemporary Tamil Nadu politics and the lives of major political figures like M.G.R.

name: T. Ramalingam Pillai
biography: A scholar who compiled one of the earliest English-to-Tamil dictionaries, a significant work that facilitated bilingual education and translation in the early 20th century.

name: T. V. Sadasiva Pandarathar
biography: A historian known for his detailed histories of the Later Cholas and Pandyas. His work was based on extensive study of epigraphic and literary sources.

name: Arul T.
biography: A contemporary poet. His poetry is known for its concise, minimalist style, often capturing a profound thought or a fleeting moment in just a few lines.

name: K.N.G. (K. N. Ganesan)
biography: A writer and scholar of the Saiva Siddhanta tradition. He has written extensively on the philosophy and literature of Saivism, making it accessible to a modern audience.

name: Kavingnar Mathi
biography: A contemporary poet and lyricist. His work often reflects social consciousness and a concern for the underprivileged, expressed in a simple and direct poetic style.

name: K. P. Aravanan
biography: A scholar and former Vice-Chancellor of Manonmaniam Sundaranar University. He has written extensively on Tamil culture, linguistics, and the history of Tamils.

name: V. C. Kulandaiswamy
biography: An engineer and academic who was a proponent of technical education in Tamil. He wrote books on hydrology and education, and was instrumental in standardizing the Tamil script for modern use.

name: K. P. Ratnam
biography: A Sri Lankan Tamil scholar and politician. He made significant contributions to the study of Tamil grammar and literature, particularly in the context of Sri Lankan Tamil.

name: S. Vithiananthan
biography: A Sri Lankan academic and folklorist. He was a pioneer in the collection and study of Sri Lankan Tamil folklore, preserving a rich oral tradition through his publications.

name: M. Ponnambalam
biography: A Sri Lankan Tamil poet. His poetry often reflects the landscape, life, and political realities of the Jaffna peninsula, marking him as a significant voice in Sri Lankan Tamil literature.

name: S. Jeyalechchumi
biography: A contemporary female writer from Sri Lanka. Her short stories and novels often focus on the impact of war and social upheaval on the lives of women and children.

name: R. Murugavel
biography: A contemporary writer and activist. His novel 'Muzhakkam' deals with the struggles of plantation workers in Valparai, reflecting his commitment to social justice.

name: M. Gopalakrishnan
biography: A contemporary short story writer and translator. His work is known for its subtle psychological insights and its exploration of the nuances of human relationships.

name: Asko Parpola
biography: A Finnish Indologist specializing in the Indus script. While not a Tamil author, his scholarly writings on the Dravidian hypothesis for the Indus language are crucial for ancient Tamil studies.

name: George L. Hart
biography: An American scholar of Tamil. His work was instrumental in the Indian government's decision to grant classical language status to Tamil. His translations have introduced Sangam literature to many.

name: Kamil Zvelebil
biography: A Czech scholar in Dravidian linguistics and literature. His extensive writings, including 'The Smile of Murugan,' are standard scholarly references on the history of Tamil literature.

name: Pa. Subramania Mudaliar
biography: A scholar and editor of the early 20th century. He was involved in the publication of several classical Tamil texts, contributing to their preservation and dissemination.

name: M. Raghava Iyengar
biography: A scholar and researcher known for his work on the history of the Alvars and early Vaishnavism in the Tamil country. His research provided valuable historical context for these texts.

name: Mu. Raghava Iyengar
biography: A distinguished scholar and historian, the son of M. Raghava Iyengar. He continued his father's work and wrote extensively on Tamil literary and political history.

name: N. Subrahmanian
biography: A historian who wrote extensively on the social and cultural history of the Tamils. His book 'Sangam Polity' is a comprehensive study of the society of the Sangam age.

name: K. K. Pillay
biography: A historian who served as a professor at the University of Madras. His book 'A Social History of the Tamils' is a major scholarly work on the subject.

name: P. T. Srinivasa Iyengar
biography: An early 20th-century historian. His 'History of the Tamils: from the Earliest Times to 600 A.D.' was a pioneering work in English on the ancient history of the Tamil people.

name: K. N. Sivaraja Pillai
biography: A scholar who argued for the extreme antiquity of the Tamil language and civilization. His work, 'The Chronology of the Early Tamils,' was influential in its time.

name: V. Kanakasabhai Pillai
biography: A historian whose 1904 book, 'The Tamils Eighteen Hundred Years Ago,' was one of the first comprehensive English-language works on the society of the Sangam period.

name: T. R. Sesha Iyengar
biography: A historian who wrote 'Dravidian India,' a work that sought to reconstruct the early history of South India before the advent of the Aryans.

name: Burra V. Subrahmanyam
biography: An archaeologist whose excavations and writings have contributed to the understanding of the Neolithic and Iron Age cultures of South India, providing context for early Tamil civilization.

name: S. Krishnaswami Aiyangar
biography: A historian who was a professor at the University of Madras. He wrote extensively on the history of South India, including the Vijayanagara Empire and the early history of Vaishnavism.

name: K. A. Nilakanta Sastri
biography: A preeminent historian of South India. His book 'The Cholas' is the definitive, magisterial account of the Chola dynasty and a classic of Indian historiography.

name: S. R. Balasubrahmanyam
biography: An art historian known for his four-volume study, 'Early Chola Temples,' 'Early Chola Art,' and 'Later Chola Temples,' which are monumental works on the architecture of the period.

name: Noboru Karashima
biography: A Japanese historian and epigraphist who was a leading scholar of South Indian history. His work focused on the economic and social history of the Chola period.

name: Burton Stein
biography: An American historian known for his work on South India. His theory of the 'segmentary state' in his book 'Peasant State and Society in Medieval South India' sparked major debate.

name: David Shulman
biography: An Israeli Indologist whose work focuses on the languages and cultures of South India. His writings on Tamil literature, religion, and history are highly influential.

name: Eugene F. Irschick
biography: An American historian who wrote on the social and political history of modern Tamil Nadu, particularly on the origins of the Dravidian movement.

name: Marguerite Ross Barnett
biography: An American academic who wrote 'The Politics of Cultural Nationalism in South India,' a key study on the rise of the Dravidian movement and its use of cultural symbols.

name: Robert L. Hardgrave, Jr.
biography: An American political scientist who wrote extensively on the politics of Tamil Nadu, including a pioneering study on the Nadars, 'The Nadars of Tamilnad'.

name: Dennis B. McGilvray
biography: An American anthropologist. His book 'Crucible of Conflict' is a detailed ethnographic study of the Tamil and Moor communities in eastern Sri Lanka.

name: Dagmar-Mina Sitaram
biography: A German scholar who has worked on modern Tamil literature. Her research and translations have helped to introduce contemporary Tamil writers to a German-speaking audience.

name: Sascha Ebeling
biography: A German scholar of Tamil literature. His work has focused on the colonial period and the development of the Tamil novel.

name: François Gros
biography: A French scholar and the former director of the École française d'Extrême-Orient. He made significant contributions to the study of Sangam literature and the Tirukkural.

name: Jean-Luc Chevillard
biography: A French linguist and scholar who specializes in Tamil grammar. He has done extensive work on the 'Tolkappiyam' and other classical grammatical texts.

name: Brenda E. F. Beck
biography: A Canadian anthropologist who has done extensive research on the folk traditions of the Kongu region of Tamil Nadu, most notably an epic folk tale, 'The Annanmar Kathai'.

name: Stuart Blackburn
biography: An American folklorist who has written extensively on the oral traditions and folk epics of Tamil Nadu, providing valuable analysis of their performance and social context.

name: Isabelle Nabokov
biography: An anthropologist who has studied the ritual and social life of Tamil Nadu. Her book 'Religion Against the Self' is an ethnography of a community in Madurai.

name: Mattison Mines
biography: An American anthropologist. His work has focused on the lives of merchants and artisans in urban Tamil Nadu, exploring themes of individuality and social change.

name: E. Annamalai
biography: A prominent Indian linguist who served as the director of the Central Institute of Indian Languages. He has written extensively on sociolinguistics and language policy in India.

name: A. K. Ramanujan
biography: A distinguished poet, scholar, and translator who wrote in both English and Kannada. He was instrumental in bringing classical Tamil and Kannada literature to a global audience through his brilliant translations.

name: J. C. Heesterman
biography: A Dutch Indologist who was a leading authority on Vedic ritual. While not a Tamil author, his work on 'The Inner Conflict of Tradition' provides a crucial theoretical background for understanding ancient Indian society.

name: Brian K. Smith
biography: A scholar of Hinduism. His book 'Reflections on Resemblance, Ritual, and Religion' explores the logic of Vedic ritual and its connection to social classification, relevant to understanding the Brahmanical tradition in South India.

name: Frits Staal
biography: A Dutch scholar who was a professor of philosophy and South Asian studies. His work explored the connections between science, logic, and ritual in the Indian tradition.

name: Franklin Edgerton
biography: An American linguist who was a professor of Sanskrit and comparative philology at Yale University. He is known for his translation of the 'Bhagavad Gita' and his work on Buddhist Hybrid Sanskrit.

name: Wendy Doniger
biography: An American Indologist whose work focuses on Hinduism and mythology. Her books, such as 'The Hindus: An Alternative History,' offer provocative and insightful readings of ancient texts.

name: Sheldon Pollock
biography: An American scholar of Sanskrit and the intellectual history of India. His work on the 'Cosmopolitan and Vernacular in History' has had a major influence on the study of premodern India.

name: Vidya Dehejia
biography: An Indian art historian and professor at Columbia University. She is a leading scholar of South Asian art, particularly the art of the Chola period.

name: R. Nagaswamy
biography: An Indian historian and archaeologist. He served as the first director of the Tamil Nadu Archaeology Department and has written extensively on the art and history of the state.

name: Iravatham Mahadevan
biography: An Indian epigraphist specializing in the Indus script and Tamil-Brahmi script. His work on the Indus script and his corpus of Tamil-Brahmi inscriptions are landmark scholarly achievements.

name: P. S. Sivaswami Iyer
biography: An Indian lawyer, administrator, and statesman who served as the Advocate-General of Madras. He wrote on legal, social, and educational matters in the early 20th century.

name: C. Rajagopalachari
biography: An Indian statesman and writer, affectionately known as Rajaji. He was the last Governor-General of India. He wrote influential English prose retellings of the 'Mahabharata' and 'Ramayana'.

name: S. Radhakrishnan
biography: An Indian philosopher and statesman who served as the second President of India. A renowned scholar of comparative religion and philosophy, his book 'Indian Philosophy' is a classic.

name: G. U. Pope
biography: A Christian missionary who spent many years in Tamil Nadu and translated many Tamil texts into English. His translations of the 'Tirukkural' and 'Thiruvasagam' are notable.

name: Robert Caldwell
biography: A Scottish missionary who was a pioneer in the study of Dravidian languages. His 1856 book, 'A Comparative Grammar of the Dravidian or South-Indian Family of Languages,' was a landmark work.

name: Constantine Joseph Beschi
biography: An Italian Jesuit missionary, known as Viramamunivar. He made immense contributions to Tamil literature, including the epic poem 'Thembavani' and the satirical novel 'Paramarthaguru Kadhai'.

name: Francis Whyte Ellis
biography: A British civil servant in the Madras Presidency. He was an early scholar of Dravidian languages and was the first to propose that they formed a separate language family from Indo-Aryan.

name: Colin Mackenzie
biography: A Scottish army officer in the British East India Company who became the first Surveyor General of India. His team collected a vast number of manuscripts, inscriptions, and local histories.

name: Mark Wilks
biography: A British army officer and historian. He is known for his 'Historical Sketches of the South of India,' one of the earliest English-language histories of Mysore.

name: Robert Orme
biography: An English historian of India. He was the official historiographer of the British East India Company and wrote 'A History of the Military Transactions of the British Nation in Indostan'.

name: James Mill
biography: A Scottish historian, economist, and philosopher. His work 'The History of British India' was highly influential but also criticized for its utilitarian biases and anglocentric perspective.

name: Henry Yule
biography: A Scottish Orientalist. He is best known as the co-author of 'Hobson-Jobson,' a historical dictionary of Anglo-Indian words and phrases.

name: Vincent Smith
biography: An Irish Indologist and art historian. He wrote 'The Oxford History of India' and several other influential works on the history of the subcontinent.

name: A. L. Basham
biography: A British historian and Indologist. His book 'The Wonder That Was India' is a classic and highly readable survey of ancient Indian culture and civilization.

name: D. D. Kosambi
biography: An Indian mathematician, statistician, and historian. He was a pioneer in applying a Marxist approach to the study of ancient Indian history.

name: R. S. Sharma
biography: An eminent Indian historian who specialized in the ancient and early medieval periods. His book 'India's Ancient Past' is a standard textbook on the subject.

name: Irfan Habib
biography: An Indian historian of ancient and medieval India, known for his work on the Mughal period and his commitment to a Marxist historiographical approach.

name: Satish Chandra
biography: An Indian historian whose main area of specialization was medieval Indian history. His book 'History of Medieval India' is a widely used textbook.

name: Bipan Chandra
biography: An Indian historian specializing in the economic and political history of modern India. His book 'India's Struggle for Independence' is a seminal work on the subject.

name: Sumit Sarkar
biography: An Indian historian of modern India. A prominent figure of the Subaltern Studies school, his book 'Modern India: 1885-1947' is a major work.

name: Ranajit Guha
biography: A historian of the Indian subcontinent who was a founding member of the Subaltern Studies Group, a school of thought that sought to write history from the perspective of the common people.

name: Partha Chatterjee
biography: An Indian political scientist and anthropologist. A founding member of the Subaltern Studies Group, his work has focused on nationalism, colonialism, and political society.

name: Gyanendra Pandey
biography: A historian and a founding member of the Subaltern Studies collective. His work has focused on communalism in colonial and post-colonial India.

name: Shahid Amin
biography: An Indian historian and a member of the Subaltern Studies group. His work has focused on the social history of the peasantry and the colonial state.

name: Gyan Prakash
biography: A historian of modern India and a member of the Subaltern Studies collective. His work has explored topics such as colonialism, science, and the city of Mumbai.

name: Dipesh Chakrabarty
biography: An Indian historian and a key figure in postcolonial theory and the Subaltern Studies group. He is known for his book 'Provincializing Europe'.

name: Arjun Appadurai
biography: An Indian-American anthropologist recognized as a major theorist in globalization studies. He is known for his work on the cultural dimensions of globalization.

name: Homi K. Bhabha
biography: An Indian English scholar and critical theorist. He is one of the most important figures in contemporary post-colonial studies and has developed concepts such as hybridity and mimicry.

name: Gayatri Chakravorty Spivak
biography: An Indian scholar, literary theorist, and feminist critic. She is a foundational figure in postcolonial theory and is best known for her essay 'Can the Subaltern Speak?'.

name: Aijaz Ahmad
biography: An Indian Marxist literary theorist and political commentator. He is known for his book 'In Theory: Classes, Nations, Literatures,' which offers a critique of post-structuralist and post-colonial theory.

name: Veena Das
biography: An Indian anthropologist at Johns Hopkins University. Her work has focused on themes of violence, social suffering, and the state, particularly in the context of India.

name: Ashis Nandy
biography: An Indian political psychologist and social theorist. His work offers a critical perspective on modernity, colonialism, and nationalism. Wrote 'The Intimate Enemy'.

name: T. N. Madan
biography: An eminent Indian sociologist. His work has focused on the study of kinship, religion, and secularism in India and South Asia.

name: M. N. Srinivas
biography: A pioneering Indian sociologist. He is known for his work on caste and social stratification in India, and for coining terms such as 'Sanskritisation' and 'dominant caste'.

name: Andre Beteille
biography: An Indian sociologist and writer. His work has focused on the study of caste, class, and power in rural India. He is known for his clear and elegant prose.

name: Dipankar Gupta
biography: An Indian sociologist and public intellectual. His work has focused on topics such as caste, ethnicity, and modernity in India. He is a frequent commentator on contemporary affairs.

name: Gail Omvedt
biography: An American-born Indian scholar and sociologist. Her work focused on anti-caste movements, Dalit politics, and women's struggles in India.

name: Eleanor Zelliot
biography: An American historian and scholar who was a leading authority on the history of the Dalit movement and the life of B. R. Ambedkar.

name: Christophe Jaffrelot
biography: A French political scientist specializing in South Asia, particularly India and Pakistan. He has written extensively on Hindu nationalism and caste politics.

name: Martha Nussbaum
biography: An American philosopher. Her work focuses on ancient Greek and Roman philosophy, political philosophy, and ethics. She developed the 'Capabilities Approach' with Amartya Sen.

name: Sunita Narain
biography: An Indian environmentalist and political activist. As the director of the Centre for Science and Environment, her writings and reports have been influential in shaping environmental policy in India.

name: Vandana Shiva
biography: An Indian scholar, environmental activist, and anti-globalization author. She has written extensively on issues of biodiversity, intellectual property rights, and agriculture.

name: Anil Agarwal
biography: An Indian environmentalist who founded the Centre for Science and Environment. His pioneering work and writings brought environmental issues to the forefront of public discourse in India.

name: Pratap Bhanu Mehta
biography: An Indian political scientist and public intellectual. His columns and essays provide sharp and insightful commentary on Indian politics, constitutional law, and society.

name: Arun Shourie
biography: An Indian economist, journalist, and author. A former minister and World Bank economist, he is known for his polemical and investigative writings on politics and religion.

name: S. Gurumurthy
biography: An Indian journalist and chartered accountant. A prominent commentator on political and economic issues from a nationalist perspective, he is associated with the Swadeshi Jagaran Manch.

name: Ramalinga Adigalar (Vallalar)
biography: A 19th-century saint and poet. Founder of the 'Samarasa Suddha Sanmarga' movement, his vast body of work, 'Thiruvarutpa', preaches compassion, universal brotherhood, and a casteless society.

name: Kavingar Mathi
biography: A contemporary poet and lyricist. His work often reflects social consciousness and a concern for the underprivileged, expressed in a simple and direct poetic style.

name: Constantine Joseph Beschi (Viramamunivar)
biography: An Italian Jesuit missionary. He made immense contributions to Tamil literature, including the epic poem 'Thembavani,' the satirical 'Paramarthaguru Kadhai,' and early dictionaries.

name: N. C. Kandiah Pillai
biography: A scholar and writer who authored several books on Tamil history, culture, and religion. His work often sought to establish the antiquity and uniqueness of Dravidian civilization.

name: K. Appadurai Pillai
biography: A scholar who compiled a comprehensive Tamil encyclopedia ('Kazhaga Thamilagarathi'). He also wrote extensively on literary and historical topics, contributing to the resources available for Tamil research.

name: Madhaviah
biography: An early pioneer of the Tamil novel. His novel 'Padmavathi Charithiram' is one of the earliest social novels in the language, notable for its realistic portrayal of Brahmin society and its critique of social ills.

name: S. R. Ranganathan
biography: While a world-renowned librarian and the father of library science in India, he also wrote on his subject in Tamil, contributing to the development of library-related vocabulary and concepts in the language.

name: Theva
biography: A contemporary writer whose stories often explore the lives of people in the city of Madurai. His work is known for its authentic use of the local dialect and its realistic depiction of urban and semi-urban life.

name: A. K. Chettiar
biography: A travel writer, journalist, and documentary filmmaker. He is most famous for producing the first documentary on Mahatma Gandhi, 'Mahatma Gandhi: Twentieth Century Prophet', and for his engaging travelogues.

name: R. P. Sethu Pillai
biography: A scholar and writer, known for his masterful oratorical and prose style. He won the first-ever Sahitya Akademi Award for a Tamil work for his collection of essays, 'Tamil Inbam'.

name: Thamarai
biography: A contemporary poet and a leading film lyricist. She is known for her refreshingly modern and poetic lyrics, which often use pure Tamil words and explore contemporary themes of love and life with great sensitivity.

name: K. V. Manaloor
biography: A writer of popular fiction. His novels, often serialized, were known for their engaging plots and focus on family and social drama, making him a household name among magazine readers.

name: M. Varadarasan
biography: A scholar and novelist, known as 'Mu.Va.'. His novels, like 'Kallo Kaviyamo', were immensely popular and conveyed moral and ethical messages in a simple, accessible style. He won the Sahitya Akademi Award for 'Agal Vilakku'.

name: Pulavar Kuzhanthai
biography: A Tamil scholar and poet. He is most famous for his work 'Ravana Kaaviyam', a counter-epic that tells the story of the Ramayana from the perspective of Ravana, reflecting the ideals of the Dravidian movement.

name: S. D. Sundaram
biography: A playwright and film lyricist. His historical plays, such as 'Kaviyin Kanavu', often had nationalist themes and were very popular on the stage. He also wrote lyrics for several classic Tamil films.

name: V. Swaminatha Sarma
biography: A journalist and writer who translated several important political works, including Hitler's 'Mein Kampf', into Tamil. He was a prominent figure in political journalism and publishing.

name: N. Chidambara Subramanian
biography: A writer of the 'Manikodi' period. His novels and short stories are known for their realism and focus on the lives of individuals in a changing social landscape.

name: T. M. Soundararajan
biography: A legendary playback singer. While not a writer, his impeccable diction and expressive rendering of lyrics written by poets like Kannadasan and Vali made him a crucial interpreter of Tamil poetry for the masses.

name: Su. Venkatesan
biography: Sahitya Akademi award-winning author and Member of Parliament from Madurai. His debut novel, 'Kaval Kottam,' is a historical epic on the city of Madurai. His subsequent work, 'Veera Yuga Nayagan Velpari', achieved massive popularity.
